title: Lentil soup
ingredients: Two 400 g tins cooked lentils, drained (or 180 g / 1 cup dried green lentils)
15 ml (1 tbsp) olive oil — swap for stock if cooking oil-free
1 teaspoon salt, plus more to taste
½ teaspoon freshly ground black pepper
Two 400 g (14 oz) tins peeled plum tomatoes
1 teaspoon (5 ml) date syrup or sugar
300 g (10.5 oz) kale or cavolo nero, optional
method: For dried lentils: rinse well, then simmer in plenty of water until tender, about 30 minutes; drain.
Warm the olive oil in a heavy-based casserole or large saucepan. For an oil-free pot, start with a splash of vegetable stock or water instead.
Add the diced onion and cook gently over medium-low heat for about 5 minutes until soft and translucent.
Stir in the garlic, minced sundried tomatoes, smoked paprika, Italian herbs, chilli flakes if using, and a pinch of salt and pepper. Cook for 2–3 minutes, stirring so nothing catches.
Tip in the plum tomatoes and crush them in the pot with a potato masher until broken down. Taste and season again.
Pour in two tinfuls of water. Simmer 45–60 minutes, stirring every 15 minutes or so, until the tomato base is thick and saucy.
Fold in the drained lentils and add enough water to reach your preferred soup consistency. Finish with balsamic vinegar, date syrup (or sugar), and more salt and pepper as needed.
If using kale, strip the leaves from the stems, chop small, and simmer in the soup for the last 3 minutes.
Ladle into bowls, or cool and chill or freeze. Garnish with parsley and a little olive oil if you like, and serve with bread.

title: Vegan meringue pie with cranberry
ingredients: Pastry: 250 g (2 cups) plain flour or gluten-free plain blend
35 g (3 tbsp) icing sugar or caster sugar
120 g cold vegan block butter, cubed
Filling: 500 g (about 4 cups) cranberries, fresh or frozen
225 g (heaped 1 cup) caster sugar, or any white sugar
2.5 cm (1 inch) fresh ginger, peeled and thinly sliced
240 ml (1 cup) freshly squeezed orange juice
½ teaspoon cream of tartar (or 1 teaspoon lemon juice)
method: For the pastry, pulse the flour, sugar, salt, and xanthan (if gluten-free) in a food processor until mixed.
Add the cold cubed vegan butter and pulse until the mix resembles coarse breadcrumbs.
Drizzle in the iced water while pulsing. Hand-mixed dough may need a little extra water.
Tip onto the worktop and gently press into a disc — add cold water 1 teaspoon at a time if crumbly. Do not knead.
Wrap and refrigerate at least 1 hour. Meanwhile prepare the cranberry curd.
Roll the chilled dough on a lightly floured surface to 2–3 mm thick, large enough for your tart tin.
Lift into the tin, press into the corners, trim overhang, and patch any thin spots with scraps.
Prick the base with a fork and chill the lined tin another 30 minutes (or overnight).
Heat the oven to 180°C / 355°F (160°C / 320°F fan). Line the pastry with crumpled baking paper and baking beans.
Blind-bake 15 minutes, remove paper and beans, then bake 10 minutes more until pale gold. Leave the oven on.
In a medium pan combine cranberries, sugar, vanilla, cinnamon sticks, ginger, salt, and orange zest with all but 2 tablespoons (30 ml) of the orange juice.
Cook gently about 10 minutes, stirring now and then, until the fruit collapses to a jammy consistency. Take off the heat and stir in the vegan butter until melted.
Whisk the cornflour into the reserved orange juice.
Discard the cinnamon sticks. Blend the cranberry mixture with the cornflour slurry until smooth.
Pour the curd into the pre-baked case (foil-shield the rim if already dark). Bake about 15 minutes at 180°C / 355°F until the surface has a slight set when touched.
Cool the pie until only barely warm. Lower the oven to 150°C / 300°F (130°C / 265°F fan) and make the meringue.
In a grease-free bowl, combine aquafaba and cream of tartar — any fat will stop the foam from whipping.
Whip on medium speed to stiff peaks (the foam should hold if you tip the bowl), usually 8–10 minutes.
Add the sugar 1 tablespoon at a time, whipping about 20 seconds between additions, until the meringue feels smooth, not gritty.
With the mixer still running, sprinkle in the cornflour and xanthan. Use the glossy meringue immediately.
Spoon meringue over the warm (not hot) filling, starting at the crust edge so it seals. Avoid trapping air pockets.
Bake 25 minutes until the meringue has a crisp, pale golden shell. Torch for deeper colour if you like.
Cool completely on a wire rack (an ice pack under the rack speeds this up). Keep the pie in its tin.
Best the day it is made; it keeps up to 2 days in an airtight box at room temperature — avoid the fridge and steam, which soften the meringue.

title: Cannellini beans with rosemary and balsamic onions
ingredients: 30–45 ml (2–3 tbsp) olive oil, used in stages
Three 400 g (14 oz) tins cannellini beans, drained
240 ml (1 cup) unsweetened soy milk or other plant milk
80 ml (⅓ cup) extra-virgin olive oil, for the rosemary oil
method: Warm 2 tablespoons olive oil in a wide frying pan. Soften the onion over low–medium heat 5–10 minutes, then add the garlic and cook until fragrant without browning.
Season, then stir in the drained beans — mash some with a fork for creaminess — along with the plant milk and nutritional yeast if using. Season again.
Simmer, stirring often, until the beans are thick and creamy.
In a separate heavy pan, heat 1 teaspoon oil. Slice optional vegan sausages on the diagonal into 1.25 cm pieces and fry until lightly charred.
Lift out the sausages. Into the same pan add onion chutney, balsamic, and maple syrup; season and simmer a few minutes until sticky and caramelised.
Spoon the hot beans into bowls. Top with sausages, balsamic onion spoonfuls, and rosemary oil. Serve with crusty bread.
For the rosemary oil: strip the leaves, trim woody tips, and chop very finely.
Warm the extra-virgin oil in a small saucepan until it shimmers, then remove from the heat and stir in the rosemary — it should sizzle without browning (test with a few leaves first).
Pour into a jar and leave at room temperature; drizzle over beans, soups, pasta, or hummus.

title: Vermicelli noodles (one pan)
ingredients: Sauce: 2 tablespoons (30 ml) soy sauce or tamari
2 teaspoons (10 ml) dark soy sauce, for colour
2 teaspoons (10 ml) maple syrup or sugar, to taste
1–2 teaspoons (5–10 ml) chilli sauce such as sriracha, to taste
Kernels from 1 corn cob, or ½ cup tinned/thawed corn
60 g (scant ½ cup) roasted peanuts or cashews
Optional tofu: 300 g (10.5 oz) firm tofu, pressed (smoked if you like)
1½ tablespoons (20 ml) soy sauce or tamari, for marinade
method: Shake all sauce ingredients in a jar until emulsified. Refrigerate leftovers up to 1–2 weeks.
Optional baked tofu: cube pressed tofu into 1.25 cm pieces. Marinate at least 1 hour in soy sauce mixed with 1 tablespoon water, turning now and then.
Heat the oven to 200°C / 390°F (180°C / 355°F fan). Drain the tofu, spread on a lined tray, and bake 15 minutes. Toss with oil and bake another 15 minutes (5–10 minutes if already well-pressed).
Cut the white and pale-green spring onion into 1.25 cm lengths; finely slice one dark-green top for garnish.
Slice the pepper into thin strips, cut beans into 2 cm pieces after topping and tailing, and strip corn from the cob if needed.
Heat a wok until lightly smoking. Add 1 teaspoon oil, stir-fry the beans 1–2 minutes, then add pepper, corn, and spring onion pieces, adding oil if the pan looks dry.
Set the vegetables aside. Pour 360 ml (1½ cups) water or stock into the wok, lay the vermicelli on top, and turn with tongs after a few seconds.
Cook, teasing the noodles apart, until the liquid is absorbed and the strands are tender with a slight bite — add a splash more water if still hard.
Toss through the sauce, return the vegetables (and tofu if using), and stir-fry briefly just to heat. Bowl up with peanuts and the reserved spring onion greens.

title: Vegan rice bowl
ingredients: 300 g (10.5 oz) firm tofu, pressed (smoked optional)
1½ tablespoons (20 ml) soy sauce or tamari, for marinade
2 teaspoons (10 ml) oil, optional, for roasting
Dressing: 2 tablespoons (30 ml) soy sauce or tamari
2 teaspoons (10 ml) maple syrup or sugar, to taste
2 teaspoons (10 ml) toasted sesame oil (or tahini or peanut butter)
1–2 teaspoons (5–10 ml) chilli sauce such as sriracha, to taste
1 corn cob or ½ cup tinned/frozen kernels (optional)
300 g (1½ cups) cooked rice of choice
Nori seasoning or crushed nori sheet (optional)
method: Cube the tofu into 1.25 cm pieces. Marinate at least 1 hour in soy sauce mixed with 1 tablespoon water in a shallow dish, turning occasionally.
Heat oven to 200°C / 390°F (180°C / 355°F fan). Arrange drained tofu on a lined tray and bake 15 minutes. Toss with oil if using and bake 15 minutes more (less if pre-pressed).
Shake all dressing ingredients in a jar until combined; keep chilled up to 2 weeks.
Julienne or finely chop the cucumber, radishes, and pepper; slice the spring onions thinly.
For fresh corn, lightly oil the cob and char on a hot griddle. Pan-char thawed kernels, or use drained tinned corn as-is.
Build bowls with rice, vegetables, and baked tofu. Finish with nori, chopped peanuts, and a drizzle of dressing (you may not need it all).

title: Savoury vegan muffins
ingredients: 90 ml (6 tablespoons) neutral vegetable oil, plus extra for the tin
320 ml (1⅓ cups) soy milk or any plant milk
1 teaspoon fine salt and ½ teaspoon ground black pepper
20 g fresh basil leaves, finely chopped
30 g drained sundried tomatoes, diced small
250 g (2 cups) plain flour or gluten-free flour blend
½ teaspoon bicarbonate of soda (baking soda)
method: Preheat the oven to 180°C / 355°F (160°C / 320°F fan). Grease a 12-hole muffin tin well with oil or vegan butter — greasing works better than paper cases here.
In a large bowl whisk together the oil, lemon juice, and plant milk.

Stir in the garlic powder, onion powder, oregano, salt, pepper, grated courgette (do not squeeze dry), basil, sundried tomatoes, and vegan feta if using. Reserve a few tomato and feta pieces for topping.
Sift or sprinkle in the flour, bicarbonate of soda, and baking powder in two additions, folding until just combined.
Divide the batter among the 12 holes and scatter the reserved toppings over.
Bake 25–26 minutes, until a skewer inserted in the centre comes out clean.
Cool completely in the tin, then loosen each muffin with a knife before turning out.

title: Roasted new potatoes with rosemary garlic dip
ingredients: 750 g (26.5 oz) small starchy new potatoes
1 tablespoon (15 ml) olive oil, plus more if needed
1 heaping tablespoon chopped fresh rosemary (from 1 large sprig)
1 whole garlic bulb plus 1 teaspoon (5 ml) olive oil
130 g (1 cup) cashews or sunflower seeds, soaked
About 100 ml (7 tablespoons) water or plant milk
1 heaping teaspoon (8 g) white miso paste
method: Preheat the oven to 220°C / 430°F (200°C / 390°F fan) and ready a large baking tray.
Bring a medium pan of water to a boil. Scrub the potatoes (leave skins on) and parboil 8 minutes.
Drain and cool until handleable, then halve lengthwise.
Slice the top from the garlic bulb to expose the cloves, drizzle with 1 teaspoon oil, and wrap in foil or a double layer of baking paper.
Toss the potato halves with olive oil, chopped rosemary, smoked paprika, salt, and pepper.
Arrange cut-side down on the tray with the wrapped garlic alongside. Roast 20–25 minutes until the undersides are golden (smaller pieces may finish sooner).
Turn the potatoes and roast 10–15 minutes more until tender throughout.

Squeeze the soft garlic cloves into a blender with the drained cashews, water or plant milk, miso, lemon juice, rosemary leaves, salt, and pepper. Blend until silky, loosening with a splash more liquid if needed.
Serve the potatoes hot with the rosemary-garlic dip.

title: Vegan spinach lasagne
ingredients: Spinach filling: 1 kg (35 oz) frozen spinach, thawed and squeezed dry
1 leek (or another small onion), diced small
200 g (1½ cups) sunflower seeds or cashews, soaked
400 g (14 oz) firm tofu, not pressed
120 ml (½ cup) lemon juice plus zest of 2 lemons
360 ml (1½ cups) soy or other plant milk
¾ teaspoon black pepper, to taste
500 g (17.5 oz) no-boil vegan lasagne sheets
Béchamel: 1 teaspoon (5 g) white miso paste
80 ml (⅓ cup) mild olive oil (or 100 g vegan butter)
80 g (scant ⅔ cup) plain flour or gluten-free blend
Salt, ¼ teaspoon pepper, and freshly grated nutmeg, to taste
method: Warm 2–4 tablespoons olive oil in a large frying pan. Soften the onion over low–medium heat, then add leek and garlic and cook until tender.
In a food processor blend the drained seeds, tofu, miso, nutritional yeast, lemon zest, nutmeg, and some salt and pepper, streaming in plant milk until ricotta-like.
Fold this mixture into the pan with the squeezed spinach and herbs. Add lemon juice and remaining plant milk; season. The filling will be quite loose.
For the béchamel: warm the plant milk. Loosen the miso with a few spoonfuls of the warm milk and set aside.
In a stainless-steel saucepan, heat the oil or vegan butter until shimmering. Whisk in the flour and cook the roux 1 minute on low–medium heat without browning.
Off the heat, gradually whisk in the warm milk until smooth, then whisk in the miso slurry, nutritional yeast, and garlic powder if using.
Return to the heat and simmer briefly, whisking, until the sauce is cream-thick. Season with salt, pepper, and nutmeg.
Preheat the oven to 180°C / 355°F (160°C / 320°F fan).
Spread ½ cup béchamel and ½ cup spinach filling in the base of a baking dish, then add a layer of lasagne sheets.
Add 1½ cups spinach filling and another pasta layer; repeat this pairing twice more.
Top the final pasta layer with remaining spinach filling, then all the béchamel, spreading evenly.
Cover with foil and bake 30 minutes. Raise the heat to 220°C / 430°F, uncover, and bake 10–15 minutes until golden.
Rest at least 1 hour before slicing so the layers set. Refrigerate up to 5 days or freeze in airtight containers.

title: Vegan broccoli pasta with chick'n
ingredients: 160 g (5.6 oz) vegan chick'n pieces or firm tofu
⅛ teaspoon fine salt and black pepper
2 teaspoons (10 ml) olive oil, for the chick'n
150 g (5.3 oz) tenderstem or regular broccoli
200 g (7 oz) orecchiette, conchiglie, or similar pasta
A few thyme sprigs, leaves stripped
Zest of ½ small lemon plus 1 tablespoon (15 ml) juice
Toasted breadcrumbs and chilli flakes, optional, to finish
method: Mix nutritional yeast, smoked paprika, garlic powder, salt, pepper, sage, and oregano (crush the herbs between your fingers) for the chick'n seasoning.
Heat a heavy skillet. Add 2 teaspoons oil, swirling to coat; add more if the pan looks dry.
Add the vegan chick'n (or tofu) and cook over low–medium heat until browned on all sides, turning occasionally.
Take off the heat and toss immediately with the seasoning mix.
Cut tenderstem broccoli into bite-size lengths, halving thick stems; or break regular broccoli into even florets.
Simmer the broccoli in salted water until just tender with a slight bite (about 2 minutes for tenderstem). Lift out, rinse under cold water, and set aside. Reboil the water.
Cook the pasta in the same water until al dente; reserve 60 ml (¼ cup) cooking water before draining.
Meanwhile, warm 4 teaspoons olive oil in a large frying pan and gently cook the garlic until soft and fragrant.
Stir in vegan cream, thyme, nutritional yeast, lemon zest and juice, and a splash of pasta water. Season and let bubble briefly.
Toss pasta and broccoli through the sauce to heat, then plate. Top with the seasoned chick'n, breadcrumbs, and chilli flakes if using.

title: Saag tofu (vegan saag paneer)
ingredients: Tofu: 400 g (14 oz) firm tofu, pressed
½ teaspoon garlic powder or 1 clove grated
2 tablespoons potato starch or cornflour (fried option)
Pinch of chilli flakes or fresh green chilli (optional)
Salt, pepper, and chilli powder, to taste
400 g (14 oz) fresh or frozen spinach
2 teaspoons (10 ml) lemon juice, to taste
To serve: cooked basmati rice or vegan naan, fresh coriander
method: Cut the pressed tofu into even bite-size cubes (about 2.5 cm).

Whisk the lemon juice, nutritional yeast, salt, turmeric, mustard seeds, cumin seeds, garam masala, garlic, and 120 ml (½ cup) water in a shallow dish. Add the tofu and spoon marinade over; refrigerate as long as possible (overnight is ideal), turning now and then.
Baked route: heat oven to 200°C / 390°F. Drain tofu onto a lined tray and bake 15 minutes; toss with 1 tablespoon oil and bake 15–20 minutes more.
Fried route: drain tofu, dust in potato starch, and pan-fry in hot oil over low–medium heat, turning, until crisp and golden.
In a large pan, wilt half the spinach with a splash of water, turning with tongs; add the rest and wilt. Lift out (leave excess liquid behind) and pulse in a food processor to a coarse mince.
Wipe the pan, heat the oil, and sizzle the cumin seeds on low heat. Add onion with a pinch of salt and cook about 10 minutes until nearly translucent.
Stir in garlic and ginger; cook about 5 minutes more.
On low heat add turmeric, chilli powder, half the garam masala, salt, and pepper; toast 60 seconds.
Add the minced spinach, vegan cream, salt, and lemon juice. Cover and simmer 10 minutes, then uncover and cook 5 minutes more.
Taste, adjust seasoning, and finish with the remaining garam masala.
Serve the saag with the tofu over rice or with naan; scatter coriander and extra lemon if liked.

title: Vegan beet burger
ingredients: 130 g (¾ cup) dried chickpeas, soaked overnight (or 360 g / 2 heaped cups cooked)
1 tablespoon (15 ml) balsamic vinegar or lemon juice
15 g mixed fresh herbs (parsley and coriander work well)
1 tablespoon psyllium husks or 2 tablespoons ground flaxseed
35 g (¼ cup) rice flour or other flour
To assemble: burger buns, sliced avocado, little gem lettuce, pickles, vegan mayo, chilli jam or sauce
method: If starting from dried chickpeas, soak in plenty of water overnight (up to 24 hours).
Warm 1 tablespoon oil in a small pan; soften the onion on low heat, then add garlic and cook until fragrant.

In a food processor pulse drained beetroot and chickpeas (use only half if already cooked) with the softened aromatics and all remaining ingredients except 2 tablespoons oil, until finely ground (chickpeas about bulgur size).
Tip into a bowl. If using cooked chickpeas, coarsely pulse the other half and fold through for texture.
Chill a few hours to firm (or freeze the mix).
Heat oven to 200°C / 390°F and line a tray. Have sesame seeds, a brush, and about 2 tablespoons oil ready.
Shape the chilled mix into patties — it will feel wet by design. Aim for about five 9 cm rounds, 1.5 cm thick (freeze at this stage if liked).
Press on sesame seeds if using, set on the tray, and bake 20 minutes, turning gently halfway.
Raise oven to 220°C / 430°F. Peel away the paper so patties sit on metal; brush both sides with oil (½–1 tsp each) and bake 10 minutes.
Turn, brush again, and bake 5–10 minutes more (35–40 minutes total) until firm. Cool briefly — they are fragile when hot.
Build burgers on toasted buns with avocado, patty, pickles, lettuce, mayo, and chilli jam. Best eaten fresh from the oven.

title: Vegan lasagne
ingredients: Ragù: 240 ml (1 cup) mushroom stock (from 15 g dried porcini or a stock cube)
½ tablespoon chopped rosemary or ½ teaspoon dried
1 teaspoon smoked paprika (more if using plain tofu)
1 tablespoon (15 ml) soy sauce or tamari
240 ml (1 cup) dry vegan red wine
400 g (14 oz) tin peeled plum tomatoes, crushed
½ teaspoon date syrup or brown sugar
500 g (17.5 oz) no-boil vegan lasagne sheets
Béchamel: 1 teaspoon (5 g) red miso paste
80 ml (⅓ cup) mild olive oil (or 100 g vegan butter)
85 g (⅔ cup) plain flour or gluten-free blend
Salt, ¼ teaspoon pepper, and nutmeg, to taste
method: Make mushroom stock with boiling water over dried porcini (steep at least 45 minutes) or dissolve a cube in hot water.
Finely dice onion and garlic; finely chop or pulse celery, carrot, and fennel until even and small.
Pulse torn tofu to a fine mince (or mash with a fork). Pulse sliced mushrooms until finely chopped with some texture left, or dice by hand.
Heat 2 tablespoons oil in a wide heavy pan. Soften the onion over low–medium heat about 10 minutes.
Add garlic and cook until fragrant.
Stir in celery, carrot, fennel, salt, and pepper; sweat about 15 minutes until translucent. Remove this soffritto and set aside.
In the same pan cook the mushrooms with salt and pepper until dark and dry.
Add 2 tablespoons oil, minced tofu, herbs, smoked paprika, and soy sauce; cook a few minutes more.
Return the soffritto. Add crushed tomatoes, tomato paste, miso, wine, mushroom stock, and bay leaves.
Simmer 30–45 minutes until the tomatoes break down, loosening with water if it looks dry.
Stir in the plant milk and simmer 5 minutes; the ragù should stay fairly moist for baking. Season, add a touch of sweetness if needed, and cool slightly.
Warm plant milk for the béchamel; loosen miso with a little of it.
Heat oil or butter in a saucepan, whisk in flour, and cook the roux 1 minute without colouring.
Off heat, whisk in warm milk until smooth, then miso, nutritional yeast, and garlic powder. Simmer briefly to a cream consistency; season with salt, pepper, and nutmeg.
Preheat oven to 180°C / 355°F (160°C / 320°F fan). Keep a bowl of cold water nearby.
Mix 2 tablespoons water with 80 ml béchamel in the dish base. Dip each pasta sheet briefly in cold water before layering.
Spread about 300 ml ragù, cover with pasta, and repeat for four ragù-and-pasta layers.
Finish with remaining ragù and all the béchamel, spread evenly.
Bake 30 minutes, then raise to 220°C / 430°F for 10–15 minutes to brown.
Rest at least 30 minutes before cutting. Keeps 5 days chilled or freeze airtight.

title: Roasted carrots with dukkah brittle
ingredients: Dukkah brittle: 1½ teaspoons (3 g) coriander seeds
¼ teaspoon flaky salt, to taste
2 tablespoons (30 ml) maple or date syrup
Carrots: 750 g (26.5 oz) small even carrots
½ teaspoon flaky salt and ⅛ teaspoon pepper
5 thyme sprigs, leaves picked, plus extra to garnish
1 tablespoon (15 ml) maple or date syrup
method: Heat oven to 160°C / 320°F (140°C / 285°F fan) and line a tray.
Optional: dry-toast the seeds until fragrant, then cool.
Crush coriander, cumin, fennel, chilli if using, and salt in a pestle and mortar to a coarse mix.
Coarsely chop the hazelnuts and combine with sesame seeds and the spice mix.
Stir in maple syrup and olive oil; spread as a slab on the tray.
Bake 10–12 minutes until golden; cool completely so it crisps.
Raise oven to 220°C / 430°F (200°C / 390°F fan) and line a large tray.
Wash and thoroughly dry the carrots; trim tops if needed.
Toss with oil, salt, pepper, and thyme. Roast about 20 minutes until a knife meets little resistance in the thickest part; remove done carrots and give others 5 minutes more if needed.
Mix pomegranate molasses with maple syrup, coat the carrots, and roast 5–7 minutes until sticky (re-glaze midway if you have leftover).
Plate the carrots with broken dukkah brittle, pomegranate arils, and fresh thyme.

title: Creamy mushroom pasta (vegan)
ingredients: 1 mushroom stock cube (or 10 g dried porcini)
125 g (4.4 oz) fresh shiitake (or extra chestnut)
300 g (10.5 oz) dried pappardelle or tagliatelle (gluten-free if needed)
4 teaspoons (20 ml) soy sauce or tamari
method: Dissolve the stock cube in 120 ml (½ cup) hot water, or soak porcini in hot water for a few hours if time allows.
Discard shiitake stems. Thickly slice both mushrooms, then pulse briefly in a processor for a coarse chop (or dice shiitake by hand and process the chestnut mushrooms).
Cook the pasta in boiling water until 1 minute shy of al dente.
Warm 1 tablespoon oil in a large frying pan; soften shallots and garlic on low heat.
Season with pepper, a little salt, and thyme (soy and miso also add salt).
Add another tablespoon oil and half the mushrooms; when they look cooked, add remaining mushrooms and more oil if needed.
Cook on low heat about 10 minutes until the mushrooms are done and the pan is dry.
Deglaze with the stock (strain porcini liquor of grit; finely chop cleaned rehydrated porcini into the sauce if using).
Stir in soy sauce, red miso, vegan cream, and 1 tablespoon balsamic. Simmer a couple of minutes; taste and add salt or more balsamic.
Reserve 80 ml (⅓ cup) pasta water, drain the pasta, and toss through the sauce, loosening with a little pasta water only as needed.
Serve with parsley and vegan parmesan or breadcrumbs.

title: Sourdough rye bread (beginner friendly)
ingredients: 150 g wholemeal wheat flour or white rye flour
method: In a large glass bowl mix the starter, wholemeal rye flour, and 150 g of the warm water to a thick paste. Scrape down, smooth the top, cover with a cloth, and ferment overnight in a warm draught-free spot until risen and bubbly.
Oil a loaf tin and dust with flour; for non-stick tins, add a narrow parchment sling for easy release.
Add the wheat or white rye flour, remaining water, salt, and most of the sunflower seeds to the preferment. Mix until no dry flour remains.
Press the dough evenly into the tin, eliminating air pockets.
Smooth the top with a wet hand or spatula. Cover with an inverted bowl and prove 2–4 hours in a warm place until the loaf domes above the rim with a few surface pinholes.
Toward the end of proving, heat the oven to 220°C / 430°F.
Gently mist the top with water and sprinkle a few reserved seeds — handle carefully so it does not deflate.
Bake on the middle shelf; optionally set a tray of warm water on the oven floor for a softer crust.
Bake 15 minutes at 220°C, then lower to 200°C / 390°F for 55–60 minutes more. The loaf is done when the base sounds hollow. Tent with foil if the top darkens too much.
Turn out onto a rack immediately so the base stays crisp.
Cool completely (ideally overnight) before slicing.
Store wrapped in paper and a cloth on the counter up to 5 days once cut. Freeze slices separated by parchment for up to 2 months.

title: Easy vegan korma
ingredients: Whole spices: 10 cm (4 inch) cinnamon stick (or ½ teaspoon ground)
4 green cardamom pods, lightly crushed (or ¼ teaspoon ground)
About ¼ teaspoon freshly ground black pepper
½ teaspoon chilli powder, to taste
1 teaspoon garam masala, divided (½ teaspoon reserved to finish)
2 tablespoons (30 ml) oil, plus extra for cauliflower
2 tablespoons (30 g) almond butter loosened with 120 ml (½ cup) water
Cooked basmati rice or vegan naan, to serve
Toasted almonds and chopped fresh coriander, to serve
method: Keep whole spices separate from the ground mix, and hold back ½ teaspoon garam masala plus nutmeg for finishing.
Warm the oil in a heavy pan over medium heat. Add whole spices and fry on low heat 30–60 seconds, stirring so they do not scorch.
Add the onion and cook gently about 10 minutes until nearly translucent, stirring often.
Stir in garlic, chilli, ginger, and a few pinches of salt; cook on low heat until soft and fragrant.
On low heat tip in the ground spices except the reserved garam masala. Toast briefly, adding a splash of water if they catch.
Add the tomatoes, one tinful of water, and salt. Crush the tomatoes and simmer about 20 minutes until fully broken down and thickened, topping up with water if needed.
Stir in coconut milk and the almond-butter mixture; simmer 5 minutes. Taste for sugar and salt. Resting overnight improves the flavour.
Finish with reserved garam masala, nutmeg, toasted almonds, and coriander. A squeeze of lime balances a full tin of tomatoes if needed.
For rice: rinse until the water runs nearly clear, then cook with 600 ml (2½ cups) water and 1 teaspoon salt under a tight lid.
For cauliflower: either simmer in the sauce until tender, or toss with oil and roast at 200°C / 390°F for 20 minutes, turning halfway, until soft and charred in places.
Warm drained chickpeas in the curry just before serving.
notes: Tags: comfort food,easy,gluten-free,healthy,Indian-cuisine. Original text rewritten for The Starred Kitchen with attribution.
credit: Rewritten for The Starred Kitchen · inspired by Ania (Lazy Cat Kitchen)

title: Masala potatoes on red lentil pancakes
ingredients: Potatoes: 650 g (23 oz) raw potatoes (or 500 g / 17½ oz cooked)
Thick vegan yoghurt or sour cream, and chutney, to serve
Pancakes: 165 g (1 cup) red split lentils, soaked overnight
Optional spices: 1 teaspoon each cumin, turmeric, and coriander, plus ½ teaspoon chilli powder
Optional aromatics: 1 garlic clove and a thick slice of ginger
Vegetable oil, for cooking the pancakes
Cashew cream: 70 g (½ cup) raw cashews, soaked 20 minutes in boiling water
½ lime, zest and juice (about 2 tablespoons)
method: Use leftover cooked potatoes, or peel, dice into 1.5 cm cubes, and boil in salted water until tender but intact (about 8 minutes for starchy potatoes). Drain and cool completely.
Heat a heavy skillet over low–medium. Add oil and mustard seeds; when they crackle, add cumin, curry leaves, and salt, fry briefly, then tip in the potato cubes.
Fry, stirring now and then, until evenly browned.
Dust with turmeric, garam masala, and more salt if needed; toss a few seconds and remove from heat so spices do not burn.
Drain and rinse the soaked lentils.

Blend lentils with salt, baking powder, chickpea flour, optional spices and aromatics, and about 300 ml (1¼ cups) water (less without garlic/ginger) to a pourable batter slightly thicker than crêpe batter; thin if needed.
Brush a reliable non-stick pan with a little oil over low–medium heat.
Pour about ¼ cup batter and spread in a circle. Cook about 3 minutes, flip, and cook 2–3 minutes more; for crispier pancakes, spread thinner and cook longer.
Keep cooked pancakes warm in a low oven while you finish the batch.
Fill with masala potatoes, vegan yoghurt or cashew cream, chutney, and plenty of coriander.
For cashew cream: blend drained cashews with lime zest and juice, salt, pepper, and about 45 ml (3 tablespoons) water until smooth (double the batch if using a large blender).

title: Vegan carrot muffins with spelt
ingredients: 150 g (¾ cup) brown sugar or coconut sugar
80 ml (⅓ cup) light olive oil or other neutral oil
2 teaspoons (10 ml) lemon or lime juice
2 tablespoons (30 ml) plant milk or water
180 g (heaping 1½ cups) wholemeal spelt flour (or oat flour for gluten-free)
220 g (2 lightly packed cups) coarsely grated carrot
50 g (½ cup) chopped walnuts or pecans
method: Stir the ground seeds with 45 ml (3 tablespoons) water and chill until gelled.
Preheat oven to 180°C / 355°F and line a muffin tin with paper cases.
Whisk sugar, applesauce, oil, citrus juice, vanilla, the seed gel, and plant milk or water until smooth.
Mix in desiccated coconut, salt, cinnamon, and ginger.
Fold in the flour with both raising agents in about three additions.
Stir through grated carrot, nuts, and stem ginger.
Divide among 12 holes, top with coconut flakes, and bake 28–30 minutes until a toothpick is mostly clean. Cool completely before removing from the tin.
notes: Tags: comfort food,easy,gluten-free,refined sugar-free. Original text rewritten for The Starred Kitchen with attribution.
credit: Rewritten for The Starred Kitchen · inspired by Ania (Lazy Cat Kitchen)

title: Roasted tomato sauce pasta
ingredients: Pinch of sugar (optional, if tomatoes are sharp)
2 tablespoons toasted pine nuts or almonds
method: Heat the oven to 220°C / 425°F.
Toss tomato halves and crushed garlic cloves in a large baking dish with olive oil, oregano, salt, pepper, chilli, sugar if needed, and basil if using.
Roast 25–30 minutes, stirring halfway, until soft, juicy, and lightly charred.
Meanwhile cook the pasta until just shy of al dente.
Tip tomatoes and juices into a blender (discard wilted basil). Squeeze garlic from its skins into the blender and purée until smooth, leaving a few pieces whole if you prefer texture.
Warm the sauce in a pan, adjust seasoning, and toss with the drained pasta.
Serve with breadcrumbs, nuts, capers or olives, almond ricotta, and herbs as you like.
notes: Tags: comfort food,easy,gluten-free,healthy,Italian. Original text rewritten for The Starred Kitchen with attribution.
credit: Rewritten for The Starred Kitchen · inspired by Ania (Lazy Cat Kitchen)

title: Vegan ramen with charred corn
ingredients: 20 g (¾ oz) ginger, peeled and sliced
½ medium chilli, roughly sliced (to taste)
360 ml (1½ cups) soy, almond, or oat milk
Coarse salt or soy sauce / tamari, to taste
4 teaspoons (20 ml) chilli oil or toasted sesame oil
Per bowl: 100 g tenderstem broccoli or green beans
Thinly sliced spring onion greens and sesame seeds, to garnish
method: Soak dried shiitake and kombu in 1 litre (4 cups) cold water as long as you can — overnight is ideal.
Brush corn with a little oil and char on a medium griddle, turning every few minutes until cooked and blistered.
In a medium pot, sauté shallots, garlic, ginger, and chilli in 1–2 tablespoons oil over low–medium heat until lightly charred in places.
Strip kernels from the cobs; reserve the cobs and split the kernels in half.
Add kombu, shiitake, soaking liquid, and corn cobs to the pot. Bring toward a simmer, lifting out the kombu just before it boils, then simmer 30 minutes.
Meanwhile steam vegetables, cook or pan-fry the tofu/tempeh, and prepare noodles separately for better control.
Remove mushrooms and cobs. Blend the broth with half the kernels, plant milk, miso, and salt until very smooth.
Return to the pot, warm gently, and season with vinegar and more salt or soy. Mirin or a spoon of nut butter can round it out if desired.
Ladle into bowls with noodles, vegetables, tofu, and remaining charred corn. Finish with chilli or sesame oil, spring onion, and sesame seeds.
notes: Tags: Asian-inspired,comfort food,easy,gluten-free,healthy. Original text rewritten for The Starred Kitchen with attribution.
credit: Rewritten for The Starred Kitchen · inspired by Ania (Lazy Cat Kitchen)

title: Vegan pretzel buns
ingredients: 250 g (2 cups) plain flour, plus extra for dusting
50 g (¼ cup) vegan butter, refined coconut oil, or liquid oil
About 300 ml (1¼ cups) lukewarm water, for the dough
1 litre (4 cups) water plus baking soda, for the simmering bath
Coarse salt, sesame, or poppy seeds, for topping
method: Combine both flours, salt, and yeast in a large bowl.
Melt the vegan butter or coconut oil and mix with 300 ml lukewarm water.
Pour the liquid into the dry ingredients and stir to a rough dough. Flour brands vary — add or hold back a little water so the dough comes together without being sticky.
Turn onto the worktop and knead 8–10 minutes by stretching and folding until smooth and elastic.
Place in a clean bowl, cover with a cloth, and prove in a warm spot (or a 25°C / 77°F oven) 1–1½ hours until doubled.
Cut eight to ten 10 cm squares of baking paper while the dough rises.
Punch down and divide into 8–10 equal pieces (about 84 g each for ten rolls).
Shape each into a tight ball, seam down, rolling under a cupped hand 30–60 seconds until the surface feels taut.
Set each ball on an oiled paper square, cover, and prove 20–30 minutes until doubled again.
Near the end of the second prove, bring 1 litre water with baking soda to a gentle simmer in a wide pot — watch for boil-overs.
Preheat the oven to 225°C / 425°F.
Lift each bun on its paper, gently flip so the seam faces up, and pinch the edges toward the centre to seal without deflating.
Simmer 2–3 buns at a time for 60 seconds per side on low heat with small bubbles. Drain on a rack.
When dry, score a shallow cross on top with a razor or sharp knife and sprinkle with salt or seeds.
Bake 17–19 minutes depending on size. Best eaten the same day.
notes: Tags: comfort food,easy,useful technique,yeast. Original text rewritten for The Starred Kitchen with attribution.
credit: Rewritten for The Starred Kitchen · inspired by Ania (Lazy Cat Kitchen)

title: Vegan pulled pork burgers
ingredients: 1 large shallot or ½ small onion, diced small
2 tablespoons (30 ml) soy sauce or tamari
200 g plum tomatoes (about half a 400 g tin)
2 tablespoons (25 g) brown sugar or maple syrup
Slaw: 150 g (2 packed cups) finely shredded young cabbage
Small handful coriander, very finely chopped
method: Wipe mushrooms clean; remove caps and slice them thinly.
Shred the stems by dragging a fork through them, then pulling into strands by hand.
Heat oil in a heavy frying pan. Soften the shallot or onion about 10 minutes until translucent and lightly browned.
Add garlic and cook 2–4 minutes until fragrant.
Lower the heat, add the dried spices, and toast 1 minute, stirring constantly.
Add soy sauce, tomatoes, sugar, vinegar, liquid smoke if using, and about 120 ml (½ cup) water. Simmer on medium-low about 20 minutes until tomatoes break down, adding water if the pan dries.
For a smoother sauce, blend this mixture then return it to the pan (or mash tomatoes fully before adding mushrooms).
Stir in all the mushrooms to coat, add about 240 ml (1 cup) water, and simmer about 20 minutes until the mushrooms are soft and excess liquid has cooked off.
Optional: chill overnight to deepen the flavour.
Heat oven to 180°C / 355°F fan (200°C / 390°F conventional). Spread mushrooms on a lined tray and bake 25–30 minutes, stirring every 10 minutes.
Combine cabbage, radish, carrot, and coriander (ice-water soak the cabbage 30 minutes for extra crunch if liked).
Whisk mayo, citrus juice, maple syrup, garlic, and mustard; season.
Dress the vegetables and taste before assembling.
Split the buns, spread with vegan butter or mashed avocado, and fill with pickles if using, pulled mushrooms, and slaw. Serve immediately.
notes: Tags: comfort food,easy,gluten-free,healthy. Original text rewritten for The Starred Kitchen with attribution.
credit: Rewritten for The Starred Kitchen · inspired by Ania (Lazy Cat Kitchen)

title: Summer farro salad
ingredients: 120 g (½ cup) dried farro (or quinoa for gluten-free)
2 small courgettes, cut into thick slices
10 g fresh basil or mint leaves, finely shredded
2–3 tablespoons (30–45 ml) lemon juice plus zest of 1 lemon, to taste
method: Rinse the farro and simmer in plenty of water 35–40 minutes until tender with a chew; drain and cool.
Brush corn with oil and grill on a low–medium griddle, turning, until cooked and lightly charred. Cool, then strip the kernels.
Oil and season courgette slices; grill undisturbed until marked, flip, and mark the other side. Cool and chop smaller.
Quarter the tomatoes; thinly slice pepper and celery; mince the spring onion.
In a large bowl combine cooled farro, chickpeas, grilled courgette, corn, remaining vegetables, and shredded herbs.
Mellow the garlic by resting it in 2 tablespoons lemon juice 10–15 minutes.
Whisk or shake garlic mixture with remaining lemon juice and zest, olive oil, maple syrup, salt, pepper, and chilli. Toss through the salad and adjust seasoning.
notes: Tags: chickpeas,easy,gluten-free,healthy,summer. Original text rewritten for The Starred Kitchen with attribution.
credit: Rewritten for The Starred Kitchen · inspired by Ania (Lazy Cat Kitchen)

title: Vegan banh mi with lemongrass meatballs
ingredients: 4 tablespoons (¼ cup) sugar or maple syrup, to taste
1½ teaspoons sambal oelek or sriracha, to taste
½ teaspoon black or white pepper
¾–1 teaspoon fine salt, to taste
About 30 g (¼ cup) rice flour or other flour
2 tablespoons (30 ml) high-smoke-point oil, for frying
Assembly: 1 crusty baguette, cut into 12 cm sections
method: Julienne the cucumber (discard watery core) and carrot, or thinly slice radishes.
Simmer rice vinegar with an equal volume of water, most of the sugar, and salt until dissolved; taste and adjust.
Off the heat, submerge the raw vegetables in the brine and pickle while you make the meatballs.
Heat oven to 200°C / 390°F and line a tray. Slice aubergine about 1.5 cm thick, bake until soft (about 25 minutes), flipping halfway; cool completely.
Bruise lemongrass, strip tough layers, and chop the tender cores. Process with cooled aubergine and all meatball ingredients except tofu until finely minced; tip into a bowl.
Pulse torn tofu to a coarse even crumb — do not over-process — and fold into the aubergine mix.
Mix in psyllium if using and about ¼ cup flour; chill at least 1 hour (add a little more flour after chilling only if still too wet).
Squeeze and roll into balls (about 20 g each). Fry in hot oil until browned all over, or bake on a lightly oiled tray at 180°C / 355°F for 25–30 minutes, turning halfway.
Split baguette pieces and toast the cut sides on a griddle or under a grill.
Mix mayo with sriracha to taste.
Spread spicy mayo in the bread, fill with pickles, warm meatballs, and plenty of fresh coriander.
notes: Tags: Asian-inspired,aubergine,comfort food,easy,gluten-free,tofu. Original text rewritten for The Starred Kitchen with attribution.

title: Giant vegan sausage roll
ingredients: 225 g (8 oz) smoked firm tofu, or 175 g (1 packed cup) cooked brown rice
1 teaspoon smoked sweet paprika (if using rice), to taste
¼ cup flour (tapioca starch or rice flour work)
Vegan wash: 2 teaspoons plant milk, 1 teaspoon olive oil, 1 teaspoon maple syrup or sugar
Gravy: 20 g mixed dried mushrooms (porcini and shiitake), rinsed
2 small carrots, scrubbed and roughly diced
method: Finely dice the mushrooms and mash well-drained tofu with a fork (hand-chop mushrooms to keep texture).
Warm olive oil in a large pan; soften shallots until translucent.
Add garlic, sage, and thyme; cook until the garlic is fragrant.
Add mushrooms and cook until tender and dry.
Stir in tofu or cooled rice, Worcestershire, soy, salt, pepper, nutritional yeast, tomato paste, mustard, and paprika if using. Cook out any remaining moisture, taste, and cool.
Mix in the flour, then pack the filling into a firm log sized to your pastry (about 20 cm). Brush lightly with oil if liked.
Preheat oven to 180°C / 355°F (160°C / 320°F fan). Bake the log on a lined tray 35–40 minutes to firm; cool before wrapping.
Take pastry from the fridge 10 minutes before assembling. Heat oven to 200°C / 390°F (180°C / 355°F fan).
Unroll pastry with the long edge parallel to the bench. Set the pre-baked log top-side down along the shorter centre.
Wrap, seal well, and carefully flip so the seam is underneath.
Score the pastry at intervals with a sharp knife, brush with vegan wash, and sprinkle with seeds.
Bake on a lined tray about 40 minutes until puffed and deep golden.
For gravy: pour about 500 ml (2 cups) boiling water over cleaned dried mushrooms and steep as long as possible.
Sauté shallots, garlic, carrot, and celery in 2 tablespoons oil until lightly caramelised.
Add tomato paste and fresh herbs; cook until caramelised but not burnt.
Deglaze with wine, then add bay, peppercorns, miso, nutritional yeast, and strained mushroom stock (save rehydrated mushrooms for another dish).
Simmer 30–45 minutes until reduced by about half.
Season with Worcestershire, soy, balsamic, maple syrup, and salt if needed; rest to infuse (overnight if you can).
Strain, pressing the vegetables. Return liquid to a pan, taste, simmer, and thicken with cornflour mixed with 2–3 teaspoons water.
notes: Tags: easy,gluten-free,Thanksgiving,Xmas. Original text rewritten for The Starred Kitchen with attribution.
credit: Rewritten for The Starred Kitchen · inspired by Ania (Lazy Cat Kitchen)

title: Cranberry vegan frangipane tart
ingredients: Pastry: 250 g (2 cups) plain flour or gluten-free plain blend
50 g (¼ cup) icing sugar, or maple syrup instead
½ teaspoon xanthan gum (for gluten-free pastry)
120 g (½ cup + 2 tbsp) solid refined coconut oil
Frangipane: 60 g (¼ cup) melted refined coconut oil or neutral oil, cooled
110 g (heaping ½ cup) caster sugar, coconut sugar, or maple syrup
½ teaspoon orange blossom water or almond extract
300 g (¾ cup) cranberry jam or jelly
method: Mix flour, icing sugar (if using), salt, and xanthan. If using maple syrup for sweetness, hold it until after the fat is cut in.
Cut solid coconut oil into the dry ingredients with a pastry blender, knives, or processor until no large lumps remain.
Rub to breadcrumbs; shake the bowl to find leftover lumps and rub those in.
For maple pastry, loosen syrup with 1 tablespoon water and add. For sugar pastry, drizzle ice water gradually (about 45 ml / 3 tbsp, more if needed) until the dough just comes together.
Press into a disc without kneading; wrap and chill 30 minutes.
Roll between parchment to 2–3 mm and line the tart tin, pressing into the corners.
Prick the base and chill the lined tin 60 minutes more.
Near the end of chilling, heat oven to 175°C / 350°F. Line with crumpled paper and baking beans.
Blind-bake 15 minutes; remove beans and paper; bake 10 minutes more.
Cream oil with sugar or maple syrup; whisk in flour; beat in aquafaba little by little.
Fold in almond meal, zest, cardamom, baking powder, vanilla, and blossom water or almond extract to a thick batter.
Cool the shell, then spread with cranberry jam.
Pipe or spoon frangipane over the jam and spread very gently so the jam stays in place.
Dot with frozen cranberries, barely pressed in.
Bake 35–40 minutes until browned (maple fillings may need ~10 minutes longer). Cool before slicing; the top crisps as it cools.
notes: Tags: gluten-free,refined sugar-free,Thanksgiving,Xmas. Original text rewritten for The Starred Kitchen with attribution.
credit: Rewritten for The Starred Kitchen · inspired by Ania (Lazy Cat Kitchen)

title: Vegan stuffed mushrooms
ingredients: A few thyme sprigs, leaves stripped
Zest of 1 lemon plus 1 tablespoon juice
35 g (¾ cup) panko or gluten-free breadcrumbs
2 tablespoons pine nuts or chopped walnuts
method: Heat oven to 200°C / 390°F.
Wipe mushrooms; remove and reserve stems.
Toss caps in 2 tablespoons oil, roast gill-side down about 15 minutes, turning halfway.
Crush whole garlic with coarse salt and dried rosemary to a paste; loosen with about 2 tablespoons oil.
Mince stems finely.
Soften shallots in 1 tablespoon oil until nearly translucent.
Add minced garlic, herbs, nutritional yeast, pepper, and ¼ teaspoon salt; cook until fragrant.
Cook the stems through in the pan.
Lower oven to 170°C / 340°F once caps are done.
Loosen miso with tray juices; fold into stuffing with lemon zest and juice.
Mix in breadcrumbs and nuts.
Add 1–2 tablespoons oil so the mix is moist but not soggy; taste.
Brush caps with garlic oil, fill, and bake 15–20 minutes until browned on top.
notes: Tags: easy,gluten-free,Thanksgiving,Xmas. Original text rewritten for The Starred Kitchen with attribution.
credit: Rewritten for The Starred Kitchen · inspired by Ania (Lazy Cat Kitchen)

title: Vegan mushroom stuffing
ingredients: 400 g (14 oz) crusty bread such as sourdough or baguette
6 tablespoons (90 ml) olive oil, plus more for greasing
5 garlic cloves (4 minced for the pan, 1 raw minced for the liquid)
1 tablespoon each chopped sage, rosemary, and thyme
120 ml (½ cup) vegan white wine or extra stock
75 g (¾ cup) toasted pecans or walnuts
method: Heat oven to 150°C / 300°F with two trays ready.
Cut bread into ~1.25 cm cubes; bake ~20 minutes, stirring halfway, until dry and hard (not browned). Cool.
Steep porcini in 480 ml (2 cups) water, or dissolve the stock cube in hot water.
Finely chop half the mushrooms; keep the rest in larger pieces.
Warm 3 tablespoons oil; soften shallots and 4 minced garlic cloves on low heat.
Add celery, chopped mushrooms, herbs, salt, and pepper; cook until browned and dry.
Add larger mushrooms and wine; simmer until wine evaporates.
Whisk soaking liquid (chop softened porcini into the pan), stock cube if unused, miso, nutritional yeast, remaining oil, and raw minced garlic.
Raise oven to 175°C / 350°F; oil a baking dish.
Toss bread in the liquid until saturated; fold in pan mixture and most nuts.
Pack into the dish, top with reserved nuts, cover with foil, bake 30 minutes.
Uncover and bake 20–25 minutes until crisp on top and moist within.
Store leftovers refrigerated airtight.
notes: Tags: comfort food,easy,Thanksgiving,Xmas. Original text rewritten for The Starred Kitchen with attribution.
