title: Vegan apple pancakes
ingredients: 2 teaspoons lemon, lime, or apple cider vinegar
2 tablespoons (30 ml) smooth nut or seed butter
About 135 ml (½ cup + 1 tbsp) plant milk
Maple syrup, seasonal berries, and thick vegan yoghurt, to serve
method: Whisk applesauce, acid, nut butter, and flax together.
Whisk in plant milk and buckwheat flour to a thick batter; thin with a splash of milk for flatter cakes.
Fold in baking powder, bicarbonate, and cinnamon.
Warm a non-stick pan over moderate heat so centres cook before outsides burn.
Brush with about ½ teaspoon oil.
Cook scant ¼-cup scoops 2–3 minutes until bubbles burst, flip, cook 1 minute more.
Keep warm in a low oven; serve with berries, maple syrup, and yoghurt.
notes: Tags: easy,gluten-free,pancakes,refined sugar-free. Original text rewritten for The Starred Kitchen with attribution.
credit: Rewritten for The Starred Kitchen · inspired by Ania (Lazy Cat Kitchen)

title: Miso mushrooms with chickpeas and kale
ingredients: 1 large banana shallot or small onion, diced small
6 lacinato kale leaves, destemmed and chopped
About 250 g (1½ cups) cooked chickpeas plus 120 ml (½ cup) aquafaba
Rice, pearl barley, or crusty bread, to serve
method: Heat 2–3 teaspoons oil in a large pan.
Brown mushrooms a few minutes, stirring often.
Add shallot, garlic, and thyme (plus oil if dry); cook until soft and fragrant.
Wilt in the kale for a few minutes.
Loosen miso with water; add with chickpeas and aquafaba.
Bubble briefly; season with pepper, lemon, smoked paprika, chilli, and salt only if needed.
Serve with grains or toast; optional almond ricotta on top.
notes: Tags: chickpeas,easy,gluten-free,healthy. Original text rewritten for The Starred Kitchen with attribution.
credit: Rewritten for The Starred Kitchen · inspired by Ania (Lazy Cat Kitchen)

title: Vegan meatball platter
ingredients: ¾ teaspoon fine sea salt, to taste
Salt, pepper, optional 1 teaspoon date or maple syrup
Crispy bread: day-old pitta or Turkish bread, oil, salt
method: Heat oven to 200°C / 390°F. Roast 1.25 cm aubergine rounds on a metal tray 25–30 minutes, flipping halfway, until soft and browned.
Pulse chickpeas to a coarse crumb; set aside.
Process aubergine with remaining meatball ingredients except breadcrumbs and oil until smooth.
Combine with chickpeas; add breadcrumbs to bind (leave wetter for baking). Chill 1–2 hours.
Roll into even balls (~21 g).
Bake at 180°C / 355°F oiled on a tray 20–25 minutes, turning once.
Or fry in ~2 tablespoons oil in batches until browned all over.
Hand-dice relish vegetables very fine; dress with oil, molasses, garlic, pul biber, salt, and pepper.
Loosen tahini with 2 tablespoons water; season with lemon, salt, pepper, and optional syrup.
Toast torn bread in 1–2 tablespoons oil until golden; salt.
Serve meatballs and bread with relish and tahini drizzle immediately.
notes: Tags: aubergine,comfort food,easy,gluten-free,healthy. Original text rewritten for The Starred Kitchen with attribution.
credit: Rewritten for The Starred Kitchen · inspired by Ania (Lazy Cat Kitchen)

title: Vegan carrot cupcakes with cashew frosting
ingredients: 200 ml (¾ cup + 2 tbsp) maple syrup or liquid sweetener
220 g (2 cups lightly packed) coarsely grated carrot
250 g (2 cups) plain or gluten-free flour
1½ teaspoons cinnamon plus ½ teaspoon cardamom (or 2 teaspoons cinnamon)
Frosting: 60 ml (¼ cup) almond milk, plus more as needed
105 ml (7 tbsp) maple syrup, to taste
250 g (2 cups) raw cashews, soaked 20 minutes in boiling water
1 tablespoon agar powder (or 3 tbsp flakes) hydrated in 90 ml (6 tbsp) almond milk
method: Heat oven to 180°C / 355°F. Line a 12-cup muffin tin with papers, or grease sides and parchment-circle the bases.
Whisk maple syrup, tahini, and applesauce; stir in carrot.
Sift flour, raising agents, spices, and salt over; fold gently until no dry pockets (avoid overmixing wheat flour).
Fill 12 cups and bake about 21 minutes until a toothpick is mostly clean. Cool completely before frosting.

For frosting, put maple syrup, lemon, vanilla, and 3 tablespoons plant milk in a blender; add half the drained cashews and blend, adding remaining cashews as it thickens (add the 4th tablespoon milk if needed). Use a spatula to break surface air pockets carefully.
Hydrate agar in the almond milk 10–15 minutes, then bring to a boil per packet directions.
Blend activated agar into the cashew cream until smooth; whisk in a bowl to remove lumps, chill until pipeable, and frost. Finish with cinnamon or orange zest if liked.
notes: Tags: autumn,baking,gluten-free,oil-free,refined sugar-free. Original text rewritten for The Starred Kitchen with attribution.
credit: Rewritten for The Starred Kitchen · inspired by Ania (Lazy Cat Kitchen)

title: Vegan raspberry mousse - 4 WAYS
ingredients: 240 g (8½ oz) fresh raspberries, plus more to decorate
2 tablespoons (30 g) smooth cashew butter (preferably unroasted)
60 ml (¼ cup) maple syrup or 50 g (¼ cup) superfine sugar
130 g (1 cup) raw cashews, soaked 30 minutes in boiling water (cashew version)
150 g (¾ cup) coconut cream from a chilled full-fat coconut milk tin (coconut version)
method: Push raspberries through a sieve for a seedless purée (under 1 cup); sieving is optional but smoother.
Cashew base: blend raspberry pulp, vanilla, cashew butter, and maple syrup (hold granulated sugar for the meringue stage if using sugar).
Add drained cashews and blend until silky; tip into a large bowl. (For coconut version, whisk coconut cream into the raspberry base instead of cashews.)
In a grease-free glass or metal bowl, whip aquafaba with 1 teaspoon lemon juice to stiff peaks.
If sweetening with sugar, beat it into the aquafaba gradually until dissolved.
Optional: mash a few extra raspberries into a thin layer in serving glasses.
Fold whipped aquafaba into the raspberry base in 3–4 additions with a gentle folding motion.
Chill until set; top with fresh raspberries before serving. Keeps about 2 days airtight.
notes: Tags: aquafaba,easy,gluten-free,oil-free,refined sugar-free. Original text rewritten for The Starred Kitchen with attribution.
credit: Rewritten for The Starred Kitchen · inspired by Ania (Lazy Cat Kitchen)

title: Vegan zucchini involtini bake
ingredients: Sauce: 600 g (21 oz / 1½ tins) quality plum tomatoes, or 750 g ripe fresh tomatoes
½ teaspoon fine salt, to taste
Filling: 135 g (1 cup) raw cashews, flaked almonds, or sunflower seeds, soaked 30 minutes in boiling water
2 teaspoons white miso (or extra salt and nutritional yeast)
3 tablespoons (45 ml) lemon juice, to taste
120 ml (½ cup) unsweetened almond or other plant milk
method: Blend sauce ingredients with 240 ml (1 cup) water — use only 120 ml if using watery fresh tomatoes.
Taste, adjust seasoning, and pour into the base of a baking dish.
Drain nuts or seeds; blend with remaining filling ingredients until smooth or slightly grainy like ricotta.
Slice courgettes lengthwise into thin, rollable strips (a mandoline helps).
Heat oven to 200°C / 390°F.
Salt and pepper the slices; rest 10 minutes to soften.
Place about a teaspoon of filling at the wide end of each strip and roll up.
Stand rolls upright in the sauce until the dish is full.
Scatter breadcrumbs if using and pine nuts; bake about 40 minutes until sauce thickens and filling is set.
Garnish with fresh basil.
notes: Tags: comfort food,easy,gluten-free,healthy,Italian. Original text rewritten for The Starred Kitchen with attribution.
credit: Rewritten for The Starred Kitchen · inspired by Ania (Lazy Cat Kitchen)

title: Pad Thai summer rolls
ingredients: Dip: 6 Medjool dates (115 g / 4 oz), pitted
3 tablespoons (45 ml) natural peanut or almond butter
2 tablespoons soy sauce or tamari, to taste
75 g (2.65 oz) vermicelli rice noodles, cooked and cooled
Small wedge red cabbage, finely shredded
Handful sugar snap peas, thinly sliced on the diagonal
method: Soak dates in boiling water 15 minutes; drain and squeeze.
Blend dates with peanut butter, 3 tablespoons tamarind, 1 tablespoon soy sauce, garlic, ginger, and about 6 tablespoons water; adjust tamarind and soy to taste.
Dip one rice paper at a time in cold water about 15 seconds; lay flat on a board.
Layer mint or coriander in the centre, then noodles and vegetables.
Fold in the sides and roll tightly from the bottom like a burrito.
Continue until filling or wrappers are used up.
Halve and serve fresh with the dipping sauce.
notes: Tags: Asian-inspired,gluten-free,healthy,refined sugar-free. Original text rewritten for The Starred Kitchen with attribution.
credit: Rewritten for The Starred Kitchen · inspired by Ania (Lazy Cat Kitchen)

title: Vegan white chocolate ganache tarts with raspberries
ingredients: Shells: 180 g (2 cups) rolled oats (gluten-free if needed)
2 tablespoons (25 g) scoopable refined coconut oil (not fully melted)
60 ml (¼ cup) almond or other plant milk
60 ml (¼ cup) maple syrup or liquid sweetener
method: Pulse oats to a coarse meal.
Mix with salt in a bowl.
Work in maple syrup and coconut oil with fingertips until a pliable dough forms.
Heat oven to 175°C / 350°F.
Press dough into tart cases.
Bake 15 minutes; press bases flat if they puff; cool completely.
Melt cacao butter in a bowl over barely simmering water.
Stir cornflour with 2 tablespoons water to a smooth slurry.
Warm almond milk, coconut cream, and maple syrup on low heat; whisk in slurry and cook until thickened.
Whisk in vanilla and salt, then stream in melted cacao butter just until smooth — do not overwhisk.
Fill shells at once; cool, then refrigerate until set (ideally 8–10 hours overnight).
Top with berries before serving.
notes: Tags: easy,gluten-free,refined sugar-free. Original text rewritten for The Starred Kitchen with attribution.
credit: Rewritten for The Starred Kitchen · inspired by Ania (Lazy Cat Kitchen)

title: Vegan new potato salad with creamy dressing
ingredients: 10 asparagus spears plus 1 teaspoon olive oil
2 tablespoons finely chopped capers, or small-diced gherkins
Pea shoots, mint, or dill, to garnish (optional)
Dressing: 150 g (1 cup) raw sunflower seeds, soaked 30 minutes in boiling water
About 240 ml (1 cup) soy or other neutral plant milk
Juice of ½–1 lemon, to taste
About ¾ teaspoon coarse sea salt (less if fine)
method: Optional: slice cold boiled potatoes into thick coins and pan-fry in a little oil until golden.
Snap woody ends from asparagus; oil lightly.
Char on a low–medium griddle (or barbecue) 3–4 minutes per side without overlapping.
Chop asparagus into bite-size pieces; season with sea salt.
In a bowl combine torn lettuce, potatoes, asparagus, cucumber, radishes, peas, capers, and chives.
Blend drained sunflower seeds with about 180 ml (¾ cup) soy milk until very smooth, adding more milk as needed.
Season with garlic, nutritional yeast, miso, lemon, mustard, maple syrup, salt, and pepper; thin to a pourable dressing.
Toss salad with dressing; garnish as liked. Dressing keeps refrigerated airtight about a week.
notes: Tags: comfort food,easy,gluten-free,healthy,oil-free. Original text rewritten for The Starred Kitchen with attribution.
credit: Rewritten for The Starred Kitchen · inspired by Ania (Lazy Cat Kitchen)

title: Vegan chocolate banana bread
ingredients: 360 g (1½ cups) mashed very ripe banana
60 ml (¼ cup) mild oil or nut butter
60 ml (¼ cup) cooled coffee or extra soy milk
175 g (¾ cup + 2 tbsp) coconut, caster or demerara sugar
180 g (1½ cups) plain or gluten-free flour
method: Preheat oven to 180°C / 355°F. Line a 900 g loaf tin; set the rack slightly below centre.
Whisk banana with oil or nut butter, soy milk, coffee and sugar.
Sift cocoa, raising agents, flour and salt over; fold from the centre until smooth.
Stir in chocolate if using.
Pour into the tin and top with hazelnuts.
Bake 45–50 minutes until a skewer is mostly clean. Cool fully before slicing with a serrated knife.
notes: Tags: bananas,easy,gluten-free,oil-free,refined sugar-free. Original text rewritten for The Starred Kitchen with attribution.
credit: Rewritten for The Starred Kitchen · inspired by Ania (Lazy Cat Kitchen)

title: White chocolate vegan sponge with strawberries
ingredients: 150 g (¾ cup) caster or coconut sugar
190 g (1½ cups) plain or GF flour
30 g (¼ cup) cornflour or potato starch
method: Heat oven to 180°C / 355°F. Line a 20 cm tin base; grease and flour sides.
Melt cacao butter over a water bath; cool.
Whisk in sugar, loosening with a splash of milk.
Whisk in remaining milk, lemon and vanilla.
Sift flour, starch, raising agents, salt and cardamom over; fold gently from the centre.
Fold in almond meal just to combine.
Pour runny batter into the tin.
Bake 30–35 minutes until a skewer is clean.
Cool the cake completely.
Stir sifted cornflour and optional icing sugar into yoghurt; chill 30 minutes.
Spread yoghurt on cake, top with strawberries and nuts. Keep chilled.
notes: Tags: easy,gluten-free,refined sugar-free. Original text rewritten for The Starred Kitchen with attribution.
credit: Rewritten for The Starred Kitchen · inspired by Ania (Lazy Cat Kitchen)

title: Easy vegan BBQ salad
ingredients: 2 tablespoons (30 ml) extra-virgin olive oil, plus more for grilling
method: Toast walnuts until fragrant; cool and chop.
Oil asparagus after snapping woody ends.
Griddle 3–4 minutes per side until tender-crisp.
Char oiled courgette strips on both sides.
Season and chop asparagus.
Season and chop courgette.
Shake dressing ingredients in a jar until emulsified.
Toss salad components; dress at the table and finish with walnuts.
notes: Tags: BBQ,easy,gluten-free,healthy. Original text rewritten for The Starred Kitchen with attribution.
credit: Rewritten for The Starred Kitchen · inspired by Ania (Lazy Cat Kitchen)

title: Vegan peanut butter brownies
ingredients: 85 g (⅓ cup) mashed banana or 75 g silken tofu
80 ml (⅓ cup) cold coffee or plant milk
150 g (¾ cup) caster or coconut sugar
80 g (⅓ cup) peanut butter, plus more to swirl
65 g (½ cup) plain or GF flour
method: Gel flax with 45 ml cold water.
Melt chocolate over a water bath.
Heat oven to 175°C / 345°F; line a 20 cm square tin with overhanging paper.
Whisk banana/tofu, flax gel, coffee and sugar smooth.
Fold in peanut butter and chocolate.
Mix in cocoa, almond flour, salt and bicarbonate; fold in flour until just combined.
Spread in tin; swirl peanut butter; add peanuts.
Bake 18–20 minutes; cool completely before cutting.
notes: Tags: chocolate,comfort food,easy,gluten-free,refined sugar-free. Original text rewritten for The Starred Kitchen with attribution.
credit: Rewritten for The Starred Kitchen · inspired by Ania (Lazy Cat Kitchen)

title: Vegan wild garlic ravioli
ingredients: 250 g (2 cups) plain flour (00 if possible)
25 g (¼ cup) almond flour or breadcrumbs
Olive oil, pesto or cream sauce; chilli flakes optional
method: Blend filling ingredients except almond flour until smooth; season.
Mix in about 25 g almond flour or breadcrumbs so the filling holds; chill.
Make a well in flour, salt and turmeric; add oil and aquafaba; bring together.
Knead at least 5 minutes; rest under a damp cloth 30–60 minutes.
Roll portions thin on a floured surface.
Form ravioli with a mould, stamp or knife; seal edges well.
Keep finished ravioli under a cloth while you work.
Boil in batches in salted water until they float and are tender.
Serve with oil, wild garlic pesto or a simple cream sauce.
notes: Tags: comfort food,Italian,tofu,wild garlic. Original text rewritten for The Starred Kitchen with attribution.
credit: Rewritten for The Starred Kitchen · inspired by Ania (Lazy Cat Kitchen)

title: Vegan burrito bowl
ingredients: Olive oil, salt, smoked paprika, cumin and chilli to coat
Spices for beans: cumin, smoked paprika, chilli, oregano to taste
2 cups cooked black beans with some cooking liquid
method: Heat oven to 220°C / 425°F (200°C / 390°F if roasting a smaller batch).
Dice peeled sweet potato into 2 cm cubes; toss with oil, salt and spices.
Spread without crowding; roast 15 minutes, turn, roast 10–15 minutes more until charred.
Soften onion in oil; add garlic until fragrant.
Toast dry spices briefly; add black beans and liquid; mash some for creaminess.
Season beans with salt and lime.
Rinse quinoa; cook with 240 ml water and a pinch of salt, covered, on low until absorbed; rest 10 minutes off heat.
Shake dressing ingredients in a jar.
Toss tomatoes, onion and coriander with half the dressing.
Build bowls with beans, sweet potato, quinoa, salsa and lettuce; drizzle remaining dressing; add guacamole.
notes: Tags: beans,easy,gluten-free,healthy,Mexican. Original text rewritten for The Starred Kitchen with attribution.
credit: Rewritten for The Starred Kitchen · inspired by Ania (Lazy Cat Kitchen)

title: Vegan carbonara
ingredients: 2 teaspoons lemon juice or 1 teaspoon apple cider vinegar
Optional toasted breadcrumbs and vegan parmesan
method: Slice mushrooms 5 mm thick; mix marinade.
Marinate mushrooms several hours, turning occasionally.
Griddle on low heat until charred both sides; chop bite-size. (Or bake 190°C / 375°F about 25 minutes, flipping once.)
Cook spaghetti in well-salted water just shy of al dente; reserve 120 ml pasta water.
Warm oil in a wide pan; gently cook garlic without browning.
Whisk cream with miso until smooth.
Add a splash of pasta water, lemon and nutritional yeast to the garlic oil; stir in cream-miso; season and thin as needed.
Toss pasta through sauce; add mushrooms and parsley.
Plate with breadcrumbs, pepper and vegan parmesan if liked.
notes: Tags: comfort food,easy,gluten-free,healthy,Italian. Original text rewritten for The Starred Kitchen with attribution.
credit: Rewritten for The Starred Kitchen · inspired by Ania (Lazy Cat Kitchen)

title: Vegan rhubarb and ginger buns
ingredients: 50 g (¼ cup) caster sugar or maple syrup
About 285 ml (1 cup + 3 tbsp) warm plant milk
Glaze: 2 teaspoons maple syrup or sugar + 2 teaspoons plant milk
Filling: 500 g fresh pink rhubarb, divided
50 g (4 tbsp) sugar, stem-ginger syrup or maple
method: Mix flour, sugar (if dry), salt and yeast.
Stir in warm milk (if using maple syrup, reduce milk by 60 ml and mix syrup into the milk first).
Bring to a shaggy dough; knead on the worktop.
Knead in solid coconut oil halfway through until smooth and elastic.
Oil the dough ball; prove covered in a warm spot until doubled (~1 hour). Meanwhile make filling.
For filling: thinly slice one-third of the rhubarb; cut the rest into 2 cm pieces, toss with sugar/syrup and roast at 200°C / 390°F about 10 minutes; blend smooth.
Deflate dough; roll to a rectangle about 36 cm wide (thinner dough = more swirls).
Spread a thin layer of rhubarb purée; scatter stem ginger and raw thin rhubarb slices on their sides.
Roll up tightly from the long edge into a 36 cm log; cut into 9–12 pieces with thread.
Set cut-side up in an oiled dish with small gaps; prove covered 1 hour. Heat oven to 175°C / 350°F near the end.
Brush with milk-maple glaze; bake 30–35 minutes until golden (foil if browning fast).
Brush hot buns with maple syrup.
When cool, drizzle icing made from icing sugar loosened with a spoon of rhubarb purée.
notes: Tags: baking,comfort food,easy,refined sugar-free. Original text rewritten for The Starred Kitchen with attribution.
credit: Rewritten for The Starred Kitchen · inspired by Ania (Lazy Cat Kitchen)

title: Vegan wild garlic pesto pasta
ingredients: 100 g wild garlic leaves (or spinach/kale + 2 garlic cloves)
70 g (½ cup) almonds or other nuts/seeds
4 tablespoons drained capers or green olives (optional)
About 120 ml (½ cup) extra-virgin olive oil
method: Wash and dry wild garlic thoroughly.
Dry-roast nuts until fragrant; cool.
Grind nuts; blend with leaves, lemon, optional capers and nutritional yeast; stream in oil; season.
Slice courgette very thinly.
Sauté in 2 teaspoons oil until just tender and browned.
Cook pasta al dente; reserve a little water.
Toss pasta with pesto, loosening with pasta water; top with courgette.
Jar leftover pesto under oil; refrigerate.
notes: Tags: comfort food,easy,healthy,Italian. Original text rewritten for The Starred Kitchen with attribution.
credit: Rewritten for The Starred Kitchen · inspired by Ania (Lazy Cat Kitchen)

title: Vegan Polish sweet cheese rolls
ingredients: 135 g (1 cup) raw cashews, soaked ≥20 min
80 ml (⅓ cup) maple syrup or sugar
80 ml (⅓ cup) plant milk if using sugar
15 g (1 heaping tbsp) mild coconut oil
250 g (2 cups) plain flour, plus dusting
method: Blend filling liquids (dissolve sugar in milk if needed), cashews and coconut oil until very thick and smooth.
Mix flour, salt, yeast and sugar.
Add most of the warm milk; adjust if using maple in the dough.
Knead until smooth, adding milk a little at a time if dry.
Oil dough; prove covered until doubled.
Punch down; divide into 6–7 balls.
Prove on oiled tray 30–45 minutes.
Heat oven to 180°C / 355°F.
Flatten; press an oiled glass to make wells; fill with cashew cream.
Brush dough with glaze; bake about 20 minutes.
notes: Tags: comfort food,easy,Polish,refined sugar-free. Original text rewritten for The Starred Kitchen with attribution.
credit: Rewritten for The Starred Kitchen · inspired by Ania (Lazy Cat Kitchen)

title: Sesame tofu onigirazu
ingredients: Flour and sesame seeds for coating
method: Rinse sushi rice until clear.
Cook with 240 ml water covered; rest; season with salt on a tray.
Pack radish/carrot in a jar; cover with boiled vinegar-sugar-salt-water brine; cool.
Press tofu.
Gel flax/chia with 60 ml water.
Mix soy, vinegar, maple, sesame oil and ginger.
Slice tofu into squares; marinate.
Heat oven to 220°C / 425°F.
Flour, dip in flax, coat in sesame; bake ~25 minutes, flipping halfway.
Place nori diamond-wise, shiny side down.
Press a square of rice in the centre with wet hands.
Layer pickles, tofu, cucumber, avocado, spinach and sauces.
Fold four corners over and seal.
Rest wrapped so nori softens; slice to serve.
notes: Tags: Asian-inspired,comfort food,easy,gluten-free,healthy. Original text rewritten for The Starred Kitchen with attribution.
credit: Rewritten for The Starred Kitchen · inspired by Ania (Lazy Cat Kitchen)

title: Vegan lemon poppy seed cake
ingredients: 150 g (¾ cup) caster or coconut sugar
150 ml (½ cup + 2 tbsp) room-temp plant milk
180 g (1½ cups) sifted plain or GF flour
4 teaspoons poppy seeds, plus more to decorate
method: Heat oven to 180°C / 355°F (160°C fan); line a 1 kg loaf tin.
Whisk oil and sugar.
Stir in milk, lemon juice and zest.
Combine dry ingredients.
Fold dry into wet from the centre until smooth.
Pour into tin.
Bake 45–50 minutes until a skewer is clean.
Cool; drizzle icing from the centre.
Whisk icing sugar with lemon juice gradually until pourable.
notes: Tags: comfort food,easy,gluten-free,refined sugar-free. Original text rewritten for The Starred Kitchen with attribution.
credit: Rewritten for The Starred Kitchen · inspired by Ania (Lazy Cat Kitchen)

title: Asian-inspired cabbage rolls
ingredients: 3 dried shiitake soaked in 500 ml water ≥8 h (optional)
220 g (1 heaping cup) uncooked jasmine rice
Dressing: 3 tbsp soy/tamari, 2 tbsp rice vinegar, 1 tbsp sugar/maple, 1 tbsp toasted sesame oil, 1–2 tsp grated ginger, 1 grated garlic clove
method: Soak shiitake ≥8 hours (or use 500 ml unsalted stock + 350 g fresh mushrooms).
Soften shallots; add garlic and ginger 1–2 minutes.
Add spices, fresh mushrooms and chopped shiitake (stems discarded); cook dry.
Season with salt and soy; stir in uncooked rice; cool.
Detach ~14 cabbage leaves.
Blanch 3 minutes in batches; ice bath.
Trim thick stems flush.
Heat oven to 200°C / 390°F.
Fill with a heaping tablespoon each; fold and roll loosely; pack seam-down.
Pour 500 ml stock over; foil-cover; bake ~50 minutes.
Rest covered 10–15 minutes.
Whisk dressing.
Serve with spring onion, sesame and dressing.
notes: Tags: Asian-inspired,comfort food,easy,gluten-free,healthy. Original text rewritten for The Starred Kitchen with attribution.
credit: Rewritten for The Starred Kitchen · inspired by Ania (Lazy Cat Kitchen)

title: Vegan brunch
ingredients: 1 small onion or large shallot, diced
method: Soften onion in oil over low heat.
Add garlic; cook 2 minutes.
Fry spices briefly; add tomatoes, salt and pepper.
Crush tomatoes; add ~500 ml water and chickpeas.
Simmer uncovered to thicken; taste.
Scramble tofu with turmeric and black salt.
Toast bread.
Serve chickpeas and tofu with avocado and toast.
notes: Tags: chickpeas,comfort food,easy,gluten-free,healthy. Original text rewritten for The Starred Kitchen with attribution.
credit: Rewritten for The Starred Kitchen · inspired by Ania (Lazy Cat Kitchen)

title: Vegan banana blueberry pancakes
ingredients: 125 g (1 cup) buckwheat, plain or GF flour
method: Mix banana with raising agents and acid.
Whisk in flour and milk to a thick batter.
Fold in most blueberries.
Warm a non-stick pan moderately.
Brush with ~½ teaspoon oil.
Cook scant ¼-cup scoops ~3 minutes; flip; cook 1 minute.
Serve stacked with maple, nuts, yoghurt and remaining berries.
notes: Tags: comfort food,easy,gluten-free,pancakes. Original text rewritten for The Starred Kitchen with attribution.
credit: Rewritten for The Starred Kitchen · inspired by Ania (Lazy Cat Kitchen)

title: Vegan yaki udon
ingredients: 100 g fresh shiitake or chestnut mushrooms
400 g precooked udon (or 200 g dry, cooked)
method: Mix sauce ingredients.
Prep vegetables into stir-fry sizes.
Heat wok until smoking; add 2 tsp oil.
Stir-fry mushrooms 1 minute; broccoli ~2 minutes.
Add 2 tsp oil; stir-fry pak choi stems, pepper, carrot and spring onion; wilt leaves.
Bubble sauce in the wok; toss with vegetables.
Gently fold in udon.
Serve with sesame seeds.
notes: Tags: Asian-inspired,comfort food,easy. Original text rewritten for The Starred Kitchen with attribution.
credit: Rewritten for The Starred Kitchen · inspired by Ania (Lazy Cat Kitchen)

title: Cauliflower salad with smoked garlic-caper dressing
ingredients: 60 ml (¼ cup) EVOO (half soy milk optional)
Olive oil; smoked paprika; nutritional yeast (optional); salt
method: Crush garlic with salt to a paste.
Mix with lemon, mustard, sugar, pepper and optional soy milk.
Whisk in oil to emulsify; add capers.
Heat oven to 200°C / 390°F.
Optional: prep and blanch leeks.
Cut cauliflower into even pieces with flat faces.
Oil and season vegetables.
Roast without crowding until charred and tender.
Plate; dress; finish with walnuts, parsley and pomegranate.
notes: Tags: comfort food,easy,gluten-free,healthy. Original text rewritten for The Starred Kitchen with attribution.
credit: Rewritten for The Starred Kitchen · inspired by Ania (Lazy Cat Kitchen)

title: Vegan chocolate raspberry tarts
ingredients: 125 g (1 cup) plain or GF flour
1 tbsp icing sugar or maple syrup
60 g (heaping ¼ cup) scoopable refined coconut oil
½ cup mashed drained frozen raspberries (~150 g)
¾ tsp agar powder (or 2¼ tsp flakes) or 2 tbsp ground chia/flax
method: Mix flour, sugar (or hold maple) and xanthan.
Cut in coconut oil; rub to breadcrumbs.
Bind with maple or cold water; chill flattened disc.
Divide into 4; roll thin; line tart tins.
Prick; chill 30 minutes.
Blind-bake 15 minutes with beans; bake 10–15 minutes more until golden.
Activate agar into raspberries, or chill chia/flax-raspberry mix.
Melt chocolate with almond milk and maple; cool slightly.
Spoon raspberry into shells; top with ganache; chill to set.
Decorate as liked.
notes: Tags: chocolate,easy,french-inspired,gluten-free,refined sugar-free. Original text rewritten for The Starred Kitchen with attribution.
credit: Rewritten for The Starred Kitchen · inspired by Ania (Lazy Cat Kitchen)

title: Vegan balsamic mushroom pasta
ingredients: Fresh thyme or ½ tsp dried
method: Heat oven to 220°C / 425°F (200°C fan).
Roast mushrooms ~10 minutes until juicy.
Toss with 1 tbsp oil, balsamic, maple, grated garlic, thyme, paprika and pepper; roast 10–15 minutes more; season with soy.
Cook pasta shy of al dente; reserve 60 ml water.
Gently cook minced garlic in remaining oil.
Emulsify with pasta water and nutritional yeast; season.
Toss pasta, then mushrooms and juices.
Finish with paprika, walnuts and thyme.
notes: Tags: comfort food,easy,healthy,Italian. Original text rewritten for The Starred Kitchen with attribution.
credit: Rewritten for The Starred Kitchen · inspired by Ania (Lazy Cat Kitchen)

title: Roasted tomato and fennel soup
ingredients: 200 g cherry tomatoes on the vine
Bread, oil and salt for croutons
method: Heat oven to 200°C / 390°F.
Oil fennel, onion, tomatoes and garlic; balsamic on onion; season with herbs and spices.
Roast 25–30 minutes, turning, until caramelised.
Simmer crushed tinned tomatoes with 1 cup stock.
Blend roasted veg (and tray deglaze) with tomatoes and stock.
Warm in pot; adjust seasoning.
Serve with cashew cream and croutons.
For croutons: dry bread cubes if fresh, then toast in oil; salt.
notes: Tags: comfort food,easy,gluten-free,healthy. Original text rewritten for The Starred Kitchen with attribution.
credit: Rewritten for The Starred Kitchen · inspired by Ania (Lazy Cat Kitchen)

title: Sweet potato and red lentil curry
ingredients: A handful of coriander, stalks chopped** + leaves for serving
1 cup of chopped tomatoes (fresh or tinned)
2 medium sweet potatoes, cut into 1.5 cm / 0.5" cubes
Approx. 1 tsp fine sea salt, to taste
Handful of cashews or coconut flakes, lightly toasted (to serve)
A good pinch of ground cloves
method: Rinse lentils until water runs clear. Optionally simmer alone in ~3 cups water ~10 minutes until soft, skimming foam.
Heat oil; pop mustard seeds.
Fry cumin seeds and curry leaves ~1 minute.
Soften onion until lightly caramelised in places.
Cook garlic, ginger and coriander stalks ~2 minutes.
Toast remaining ground spices (hold garam masala) 1–2 minutes on low heat.
Add tomatoes + 240 ml water; cover until soft.
Add lentils (if not pre-cooked), sweet potato + ~500 ml water.
Simmer covered until potato is tender; add water if dry.
Stir in salt, coconut milk and any pre-cooked lentils; simmer 5 minutes.
Finish with garam masala and lime.
Serve with rice or naan, coriander and toasted nuts.
notes: Tags: coconut,easy,gluten-free,Indian-cuisine. Original text rewritten for The Starred Kitchen with attribution.
credit: Rewritten for The Starred Kitchen · inspired by Ania (Lazy Cat Kitchen)

title: Simplest vegan pasta ever
ingredients: 200 g / 7 oz spaghetti or rigatoni pasta (use GF for gluten-free version)
A good pinch of chilli flakes , optional or black pepper, to taste
method: Cook pasta just under al dente; save cooking water.
Soften garlic in olive oil on very low heat without colouring.
Emulsify nutritional yeast with ~2 tbsp pasta water and 1 tbsp caper brine; bubble briefly.
Toss pasta with minced capers and parsley; salt only if needed.
Plate with chilli or pepper.
notes: Tags: comfort food,easy,gluten-free,Italian. Original text rewritten for The Starred Kitchen with attribution.
credit: Rewritten for The Starred Kitchen · inspired by Ania (Lazy Cat Kitchen)

title: Healthy date bars
ingredients: 25 g / ¼ cup ground flax seeds
3 tbsp maple syrup (skip if using 250 g / 9 oz dates)
method: Pit and soak dates 20 minutes in boiling water.
Line a small tin; heat oven to 150°C / 300°F.
Mix nuts, seeds, puffed rice, flax and cardamom.
Blend dates with vanilla and tahini (+ only 2 tbsp boiling water) to a thick paste; reserve ¼ cup if needed for topping.
Work paste into dry mix by hand.
Press firmly into the tin.
Bake 30–40 minutes until browned.
Compress and weight while cooling.
Melt coconut oil; mix with cocoa and maple or date paste.
Spread on bars; sesame and salt; chill.
Slice and store airtight.
notes: Tags: easy,gluten-free,healthy,refined sugar-free Nearly raw / no-bake style. Original text rewritten for The Starred Kitchen with attribution.
credit: Rewritten for The Starred Kitchen · inspired by Ania (Lazy Cat Kitchen)

title: Easy chana masala
ingredients: 2 tablespoon (30 ml) oil, for example coconut oil
½ tsp amchoor / dried mango powder (or squeeze of lemon at the end)
½ tsp chilli powder , to taste
Two 400g / 14 oz tins quality plum tomatoes*, crushed so they cook quicker
1 tsp date syrup, store-bought or homemade or sugar (optional)
Cooked rice or a vegan naan, to serve
method: Soft-fry onion in oil on low heat.
Combine dry spices except ½ tsp garam masala.
Add garlic, ginger and curry leaves until aromatic.
Toast ground spices 1–2 minutes on very low heat.
Add tomatoes, chickpeas, salt and ~2 tinfuls water; simmer 45–60 minutes (lid 30 min, then reduce).
Stir in reserved garam masala (+ lemon if no amchoor).
Adjust seasoning; serve with rice/naan and coriander.
notes: Tags: chickpeas,comfort food,easy,gluten-free,healthy. Original text rewritten for The Starred Kitchen with attribution.
credit: Rewritten for The Starred Kitchen · inspired by Ania (Lazy Cat Kitchen)

title: Baked vegan hash browns
ingredients: 450 g / 1 lb starchy variety potatoes , peeled
1 large shallot or ½ large onion, finely grated or chopped
A good grind of black pepper, to taste
method: Optional: parboil potatoes 5 minutes and cool for softer centres (raw = crispier).
Coarsely grate potatoes.
Oven 180°C / 355°F (raw) or 200°C / 390°F (parboiled); ready tray and 8 cm ring.
Mix with shallot, salt, pepper; rest raw mix 10 minutes.
Squeeze raw potato dry.
Oil tray; pack mix in ring; lift.
Bake ~20 min raw or ~10 min parboiled; flip, oil, finish golden.
Serve immediately with vegan sour cream or ketchup.
notes: Tags: comfort food,easy,gluten-free,healthy. Original text rewritten for The Starred Kitchen with attribution.
credit: Rewritten for The Starred Kitchen · inspired by Ania (Lazy Cat Kitchen)

title: Gochujang tempeh
ingredients: 2-3 tbsp high smoke point oil, optional
2 tbsp soy sauce or tamari (for GF version)
2 tbsp maple syrup (or sugar dissolved in soy sauce)
Approx. 2 tbsp natural vegan yoghurt , optional
2 tbsp toasted and crushed peanuts, to serve
Small wedge of red cabbage, shredded very finely
1 spring onion / scallion, chopped very finely (green part saved for garnish)
method: Steam or simmer tempeh halves 15 minutes; drain.
Tear into rustic chunks.
Bake path: oven 200°C / 390°F on a lined tray.
Fry path: brown in 2 tbsp hot oil.
Whisk marinade from gochujang through ginger; taste.
Reserve 2 tbsp; coat tempeh; marinate.
Bake at 200°C / 390°F, basting, until sticky.
Toss julienned vegetables and cabbage with coriander and spring onion whites.
Dress with seasoned vinegar, sesame oil and salt; rest ≥20 minutes. Serve over rice with peanuts and greens.
notes: Tags: Asian-inspired,comfort food,gluten-free,healthy. Original text rewritten for The Starred Kitchen with attribution.
credit: Rewritten for The Starred Kitchen · inspired by Ania (Lazy Cat Kitchen)

title: Soft vegan gingerbread cookies
ingredients: 250 g / 2 cups all purpose flour OR a tried and tested GF flour mix
50g - 100g / ¼ - ½ cup sugar*, coconut sugar for refined sugar-free version
50 g / 60 ml / ¼ cup melted refined coconut oil or other neutral tasting oil
60 ml / ¼ cup smooth (not chunky!) applesauce
120 ml / ½ cup maple syrupICING 125 g / 1 cup icing sugar
method: Whisk flour, sugar, yeast, raising agents, cocoa, spices and salt.
Stir melted oil, applesauce and maple syrup together.
Combine wet and dry; knead gently into a dough.
Halve and refrigerate 30 minutes.
Heat oven to 175°C / 350°F; line two trays.
Warm dough slightly; roll and cut. Group similar sizes.
Bake small cookies 7–8 minutes, larger 9–10 — longer for crispier.
Mix icing sugar with ~1 tbsp water to a thick paste.
Pipe from a snipped bag; let set before storing.
notes: Tags: easy,gluten-free,Xmas. Original text rewritten for The Starred Kitchen with attribution.
credit: Rewritten for The Starred Kitchen · inspired by Ania (Lazy Cat Kitchen)

title: Vegan mushroom risotto
ingredients: 40 g / 1.4 oz dry porcini* OR a mixture of porcini and shiitake
750 g / 26 oz preferred fresh mushrooms (shiitake, chestnut / cremini, oyster)
4 small shallots or ½ large onion, diced small
3 large garlic cloves, 2 diced small and 1 finely grated
120 ml / ½ cup vegan white wine
Approx. 2 cups / 500 ml veggie stock, from a stock cube or homemade vegan stock
Salt and black pepper, to taste
35 g / ¼ cup cashews soaked in boiling water for 30 min (optional)
2-3 sprigs of fresh thyme, leaves only
Well minced fresh parsley, to garnish
method: Rinse dried mushrooms; steep in 500 ml boiling water ~30 minutes.
Wipe fresh mushrooms dry; slice.
Warm 2 tbsp oil in a lidded heavy pan.
Soft-fry shallots ~5 minutes until translucent.
Add 2 minced garlic cloves; cook ~2 minutes.
Toast rice a few seconds, stirring.
Strain mushroom stock (leave grit behind); keep hot. Save rehydrated mushrooms.
Deglaze with wine; cook off, then add hot stock a ladle at a time, stirring.
Continue adding stock as absorbed (~15–20 minutes) until rice is almost al dente; use veg stock if needed.
Optional: blend soaked cashews with some rehydrated porcini and water to a cream.
Pan-fry fresh mushrooms in batches in oil until caramelised.
When rice is nearly ready, fold in porcini cream and optional balsamic; cover off heat 5 minutes.
Spoon into bowls; top with mushrooms and parsley.
notes: Tags: comfort food,easy,gluten-free,Italian. Original text rewritten for The Starred Kitchen with attribution.
credit: Rewritten for The Starred Kitchen · inspired by Ania (Lazy Cat Kitchen)

title: Vegan potato gratin
ingredients: 150 g / 1 cup raw cashews (soaked in boiling water for 1 hr)
420 ml / 1¾ cups unsweetened almond or oat milk
1 tbsp lemon juice or apple cider vinegar, to taste
1 heaped tbsp white miso paste (use GF miso if required)
2 sprigs of fresh rosemary, leaves only
4 sprigs of fresh thyme, leaves only
¼ tsp ground nutmeg, to taste
1/8 tsp cayenne pepper, to taste (skip if you don't like heat)
Generous amount of black pepper, to taste
Approx. 1¾ tsp sea salt flakes , to taste
Approx. 2 kg / 4.4 lb starchy potatoes (russet or Maris Piper)
method: Blend drained cashews with 240 ml plant milk until silky.
Blend in remaining sauce ingredients through salt; adjust (it mellows when baked). Tip into a large bowl.
Oil a baking dish; heat oven to 200°C / 390°F.
Wash, dry and mandoline-slice potatoes 3 mm thick.
Toss slices in the sauce to coat.
Stand slices vertically, packing tightly with jagged tops.
Pour remaining sauce halfway up; cover with foil.
Bake 30 minutes covered, then 45–60 minutes uncovered until crisp and tender. Rest briefly.
notes: Tags: comfort food,easy,french-inspired,gluten-free. Original text rewritten for The Starred Kitchen with attribution.
credit: Rewritten for The Starred Kitchen · inspired by Ania (Lazy Cat Kitchen)

title: Vegan pumpkin pie
ingredients: 180 g / 1½ cups all purpose flour OR GF all purpose flour mix
½ tsp xanthan gum (for GF version only)
100 g / ½ cup solid (not melted) mild coconut oil, chopped up small
90 ml / ¼ cup + 2 tbsp smooth almond butter
1/8 tsp ground cloves or all spice
Thick dairy-free yoghurt or whipped coconut cream
method: Mix flour, salt and xanthan (if GF).
Cut in solid coconut oil to a sandy mix.
Trickle in ice water until dough holds; press into a disc; chill 30–45 minutes.
Roll on floured surface or between parchment (press GF dough into tin by hand if easier).
Line a ~24 cm pie dish; fold excess under for a thick rim.
Heat oven to 160°C fan / 180°C conventional; freeze lined shell 15 minutes.
Blind-bake with paper and beans 10–15 minutes.
Remove weights; bake 10 minutes more.
Blend filling ingredients until smooth.
Fill the shell.
Bake 35–40 minutes until edges set and centre slightly soft.
Cool completely before slicing.
Top with yoghurt or coconut cream and cinnamon.
notes: Tags: comfort food,gluten-free,refined sugar-free,Thanksgiving,tofu. Original text rewritten for The Starred Kitchen with attribution.
credit: Rewritten for The Starred Kitchen · inspired by Ania (Lazy Cat Kitchen)

title: Roasted sweet potatoes with miso sauce
ingredients: 1 tbsp seasoned rice vinegar or lime juice
2 tsp maple syrup or coconut sugar
Bunch of fresh coriander, finely chopped
2 tbsp toasted almonds or almond flakes
method: Whisk miso, vinegar or lime, maple, sriracha and yoghurt with a splash of water to a glossy sauce.
Heat oven to 220°C / 425°F.
Scrub sweet potatoes; trim blemishes.
Cut into slim wedges.
Oil cut sides; roast cut-side down 12–15 minutes; turn until tender.
Plate; drizzle sauce; finish with coriander and toasted almonds.
notes: Tags: easy,gluten-free,healthy. Original text rewritten for The Starred Kitchen with attribution.
credit: Rewritten for The Starred Kitchen · inspired by Ania (Lazy Cat Kitchen)

title: Easy vegan chocolate cookies
ingredients: 100 g / 3.5 oz vegan 70% cocoa dark chocolate
80 ml / 1/3 cup aquafaba (chickpea brine), from a tin or from homecooked chickpeas
140 g / 2/3 cup sugar (caster sugar gives you the crispiest outer shell, but coconut sugar works well too!)
80 g / 1/3 cup 100% natural nut or seed butter of choice
100 g / 1 cups finely ground almonds / almond flour
¼ tsp salt OR coarse sea salt for sprinkling
½ tsp baking soda (GF certified if needed)
method: Melt chocolate slowly over a water bath.
Heat oven to 175°C / 345°F; line a tray.
Whip aquafaba until foamy.
Beat in sugar gradually.
Fold in warm melted chocolate.
Fold in nut or seed butter.
Fold in dry ingredients in batches.
Scoop ~2 tbsp mounds with space; add salt flakes if using.
Bake mid-oven 10–11 minutes; cool completely.
notes: Tags: aquafaba,baking,chocolate,comfort food,easy,gluten-free. Original text rewritten for The Starred Kitchen with attribution.
credit: Rewritten for The Starred Kitchen · inspired by Ania (Lazy Cat Kitchen)

title: Vegan pumpkin galette
ingredients: 60 ml / ¼ cup thick vegan yoghurt
1½ tsp apple cider vinegar (or other acid)
150 g / slightly heaped 1¼ cups spelt flour
75 g / 1/3 cup solid (not melted!) refined coconut oil, chopped up into small pieces
500 g / 18 oz peeled and cored pumpkin or squash
½-1 raw garlic clove, finely grated
Vegan feta or cashew ricotta, to decorate (optional)
method: Mix yoghurt, vinegar and 35 ml cold water; chill. Mix flour and salt.
Cut solid coconut oil into flour to breadcrumbs.
Rub until even.
Add yoghurt mix; bring dough together without kneading; chill.
Heat oven to 190°C / 375°F; toss pumpkin with oil.
Roast ~30 minutes until soft, stirring once.
Process or mash tofu filling until spreadable.
Slow-cook thick onion slices in oil ~20 minutes.
Add salt, balsamic and sugar; caramelise 5–10 minutes more.
Roll chilled pastry on floured parchment to a rough circle.
Spread filling with a border; top with pumpkin and onions.
Fold edges over; brush with sweetened soy milk.
Bake at 200°C / 390°F 40–45 minutes.
Cool slightly; finish with thyme and vegan cheese if liked.
notes: Tags: baking,butternut squash,comfort food,easy. Original text rewritten for The Starred Kitchen with attribution.
credit: Rewritten for The Starred Kitchen · inspired by Ania (Lazy Cat Kitchen)

title: Vegan shepherd's pie
ingredients: 12 g / 0.4 oz dried porcini mushrooms (optional, but recommended)
250 g / 10 oz chestnut mushrooms, diced small
120 ml / ½ cup vegan red wine (or vegan stock)
2 cups soaked overnight (raw) chickpeas or cooked chickpeas
Two 400 g / 14 oz tins quality peeled plum tomatoes
1 tsp date syrup or sugar (optional, to taste)
4 tbsp extra virgin olive oil or vegan butter, plus extra to drizzle
Approx. 240 ml / 1 cup unsweetened almond milk or cashew cream*** (for extra indulgence)
Approx. ½ tsp salt, more to taste
A good pinch of grated nutmeg, to taste
method: Rinse dried porcini; cover with boiling water.
Soft-fry onion in oil until nearly translucent.
Add garlic 1–2 minutes.
Sauté celery, carrot and chestnut mushrooms ~5 minutes.
Finely chop rehydrated porcini (keep liquid).
Add porcini, herbs, bay, smoked paprika and seasoning.
Pour in strained mushroom stock.
Simmer; add wine and bubble a few minutes.
Pulse chickpeas to a mince-like texture.
Add tomatoes and ~240 ml water.
Simmer covered until tomatoes break down.
Uncover and reduce.
Season with salt, optional sweetness and pepper.
Boil potatoes until tender.
Mash or rice until smooth.
Beat in fat, plant milk and seasoning until fluffy.
Heat oven to 225°C / 435°F.
Spread mince; top with potato; brush with oil.
Bake ~30 minutes until golden; rest for neater slices.
notes: Tags: comfort food,easy,gluten-free,healthy,winter. Original text rewritten for The Starred Kitchen with attribution.
credit: Rewritten for The Starred Kitchen · inspired by Ania (Lazy Cat Kitchen)

title: Vegan pumpkin alfredo
ingredients: 400 g / 14 oz rigatoni (or other similar pasta shape)
Approx. 220 g / 1 cup pureed / fork smashed cooked or roasted pumpkin
60 ml / ¼ cup homemade cashew cream**, Oatly or similar plant-based cream
method: Roast hazelnuts at 175°C / 345°F about 8 minutes.
Rub in a towel to loosen skins; crush some for garnish.
Cook pasta until 2 minutes shy of done; reserve water.
Fry sage leaves flat in oil until crisp; drain.
Gently cook garlic in the same oil.
Whisk in nutritional yeast and ~2 tbsp pasta water.
Add pumpkin, miso, cream, vinegar and spices; thin as needed.
Taste; optionally blend smooth.
Toss pasta in the sauce to heat.
Serve with fried sage and hazelnuts.
notes: Tags: easy,gluten-free,healthy,Italian. Original text rewritten for The Starred Kitchen with attribution.
credit: Rewritten for The Starred Kitchen · inspired by Ania (Lazy Cat Kitchen)

title: Plant bolognese sauce
ingredients: 100 g / 1½ cups non-GMO soy mince (also known as textured vegetable protein or TVP)
2 short celery stalks, very diced small
125 g / 5 oz chestnut mushrooms, diced small
120 ml / ½ cup vegan red wine
Two 400 g / 28 oz tins quality peeled plum tomatoes
1 tsp date syrup or sugar (optional, to taste)
Fresh thyme or parsley, to garnish
500 g / 18 oz dry tagliatelle (GF if required), cooked
method: Boil a kettle. Rinse dried mushrooms and place in a bowl.
Cover with boiling water; set aside.
In another bowl cover soy mince with boiling water.
Soft-fry onion in olive oil until nearly translucent.
Add garlic 1–2 minutes.
Sauté celery, carrot and chestnut mushrooms ~5 minutes.
Finely chop rehydrated mushrooms (keep liquid).
Add chopped mushrooms, rosemary, thyme and smoked seasoning.
Pour in strained mushroom stock.
Simmer; add wine and bubble a few minutes.
Add stock cube, tomatoes and ~240 ml water.
Simmer covered until tomatoes soften.
Stir in drained soy mince halfway through.
Uncover and reduce until rich.
Season with salt, optional sweetness and pepper.
notes: Tags: comfort food,easy,gluten-free,Italian. Original text rewritten for The Starred Kitchen with attribution.
credit: Rewritten for The Starred Kitchen · inspired by Ania (Lazy Cat Kitchen)

title: Vegan apple muffins
ingredients: 150 g / ¾ cup brown sugar or 180 ml / ¾ cup maple syrup
120 ml / ½ cup almond milk (decrease to 60 ml / ¼ cup if using maple syrup)
50 g / 60 ml / ¼ cup softened coconut oil or 60 g / 60 ml / ¼ cup almond butter (for oil-free version)
200 g / 2 cups oat flour (GF certified if needed)
100 g / 1 slightly heaped cup finely ground almonds / almond flour
¾ tsp baking soda (GF certified if needed)
1½ tsp baking powder (GF certified if needed)
3 cardamon pods (¼ tsp ground), crushed in a pestle and mortar
Flaked almonds or blackberries, for topping
method: Heat oven to 180°C / 355°F; lightly oil a 12-hole tin.
Whisk sugar, almond milk, applesauce, oil and vanilla.
Mix oat flour, almond flour, salt, raising agents and spices.
Sift dry into wet; fold until combined.
Fold in diced apple; divide among 12 holes.
Top with almond flakes or a blackberry.
Bake 25–30 minutes (maple versions may need ~5 minutes more); cool before removing.
notes: Tags: baking,easy,gluten-free,oil-free,refined sugar-free. Original text rewritten for The Starred Kitchen with attribution.
credit: Rewritten for The Starred Kitchen · inspired by Ania (Lazy Cat Kitchen)

title: Vegan curry with green beans
ingredients: ¼ cup toasted or untoasted coconut flakes
8 dry (or fresh ones if you can find them) curry leaves
½ tsp Kashmiri (adds bright red colour) or regular chilli powder, adjust to your tolerance
¼ tsp ground black (or white pepper)
400 g / 14 oz tomatoes (3 medium), peeled and chopped
75 g / ½ cup petit pois or green peas
120 ml / ½ cup full fat coconut milk
method: Toast coconut flakes until golden if not already toasted.
Pop mustard seeds in hot oil.
Fry fennel seeds and curry leaves 1–2 minutes.
Soften onion 5–7 minutes.
Add garlic and ginger until fragrant.
Toast dry spices briefly in the aromatics.
Add tomatoes, ~240 ml water and ½ tsp salt.
Simmer covered until tomatoes collapse.
Meanwhile steam broccoli 7–8 minutes and green beans 5–7 minutes.
Boil peas 2 minutes; char oiled courgette on a griddle.
Stir coconut milk into the sauce; simmer gently.
Adjust salt, sugar and lime.
Serve over rice with coriander and toasted coconut.
notes: Tags: comfort food,easy,gluten-free,healthy,Indian-cuisine. Original text rewritten for The Starred Kitchen with attribution.
credit: Rewritten for The Starred Kitchen · inspired by Ania (Lazy Cat Kitchen)

title: Vegan blueberry muffins
ingredients: 150 g / ¾ cup brown sugar or coconut sugar
300 ml / 1¼ cup almond milk or other thin plant milk
2 tsp lemon or lime juice (or apple cider vinegar)
240 g / 2 cups all purpose wheat flour or a reliable GF flour mix
80 g / ¾ cup finely ground almonds / almond flour
¾ tsp baking soda (GF certified if needed)
1 tsp baking powder (GF certified if needed)
method: Heat oven to 180°C / 355°F; line or grease a 12-hole tin.
Beat almond butter, sugar and a splash of almond milk smooth.
Whisk in remaining milk, lemon juice, vanilla and almond extract.
Sift dry ingredients over; fold gently.
Fold in most blueberries.
Divide among cups; top with remaining berries.
Bake 25–30 minutes until a toothpick is clean; cool completely.
notes: Tags: baking,comfort food,gluten-free,oil-free,refined sugar-free. Original text rewritten for The Starred Kitchen with attribution.
credit: Rewritten for The Starred Kitchen · inspired by Ania (Lazy Cat Kitchen)

title: Fennel and roasted cherry salad
ingredients: 250 g / 9 oz fennel (1 large), a couple of fronds reserved and chopped finely
2 tablespoon (30 ml) extra virgin olive oil, divided
Sea salt and black pepper, to taste
1 tbsp raw apple vinegar or lemon juice
method: Toast almond flakes until golden, stirring often; cool.
Heat oven to 200°C / 390°F.
Toss pitted cherries with 1 tsp oil, 1 tsp maple and thyme.
Roast 20–25 minutes, stirring halfway.
Core fennel; slice paper-thin on a mandoline.
Whisk remaining oil with vinegar, mustard, minced shallot, salt and pepper.
Dress fennel on a platter; add cherries and juices; finish with herbs, almonds and optional cheese.
notes: Tags: easy,french-inspired,gluten-free,healthy. Original text rewritten for The Starred Kitchen with attribution.
credit: Rewritten for The Starred Kitchen · inspired by Ania (Lazy Cat Kitchen)

title: Vegan beetroot risotto
ingredients: 2½ tablespoon (40 ml) extra virgin olive oil, plus more for grilling
¾ tsp salt, more to taste
Freshly ground black pepper, to taste
3 small shallots or ½ large onion, diced small
120 ml / ½ cup vegan white wine
A few sprigs of fresh thyme, leaves picked
1 vegan stock cube dissolved in 3 cups / 750 ml water or homemade vegan stock
method: Heat oven to 200°C / 390°F.
Peel beetroots; dice one small (or grate); cut others into wedges.
Oil and season wedges; roast until tender.
Warm 2 tbsp oil in a lidded pan.
Soft-fry shallots ~5 minutes.
Keep stock hot in a separate pot.
Add garlic ~2 minutes.
Toast rice briefly.
Add diced beetroot, wine, nutritional yeast, salt, pepper and thyme.
Add hot stock ladle by ladle, stirring as absorbed.
Cook until rice is almost al dente (~15–20 minutes).
Off heat, cover and rest 5 minutes.
Reduce balsamic with maple until syrupy.
Serve risotto topped with roasted beets, balsamic glaze and optional cream.
notes: Tags: beetroot,comfort food,easy,gluten-free. Original text rewritten for The Starred Kitchen with attribution.
credit: Rewritten for The Starred Kitchen · inspired by Ania (Lazy Cat Kitchen)

title: Easy vegan ricotta cheese - 2 ways
ingredients: 90 ml / ¼ cup + 2 tbsp unsweetened plant milk
2 tbsp lemon juice OR 2 tbsp plant milk and 1 vegan probiotic capsule
Approx. ¼-½ tsp salt, to taste and application (i.e. sweet vs savoury)
method: Quick ricotta: soak cashews overnight or 30 minutes in boiling water; drain.
Put plant milk and lemon juice in a blender.
Blend cashews in two additions until smooth.
Use a spatula to keep the mixture moving if the blender stalls.
Season with salt and optional nutritional yeast.
Hang in muslin over a sieve until thickened to ricotta texture.
Cultured version: soak and drain cashews as above.
Blend with 120 ml plant milk until smooth.
Keep blending until silky.
Season with salt and nutritional yeast.
Stir in probiotic powder in a non-metal bowl.
Hang in muslin at room temperature 24–72 hours until tangy and set.
Chill before using.
notes: Tags: easy,gluten-free,healthy,oil-free,useful technique. Original text rewritten for The Starred Kitchen with attribution.
credit: Rewritten for The Starred Kitchen · inspired by Ania (Lazy Cat Kitchen)

title: Vegan mince stuffed eggplants
ingredients: 3 small shallots or 1 small onion, diced finely
A good pinch of hot chilli (optional)
½-¾ tsp salt, more to taste
½ x 400 g / 14 oz can of plum tomatoes or 2 ripe tomatoes, peeled and chopped
1 cup cooked firm variety of lentils*
75 g / ¾ cup walnut pieces**, finely chopped
½-1 tsp date syrup or sugar
1 tbsp toasted pine nuts, to garnish (optional)
method: Halve aubergines lengthwise; score flesh in a crosshatch without piercing skin.
Brush a griddle with 2 tsp oil; char cut-side down until soft (or bake).
Warm remaining 2 tbsp oil in a heavy pan.
Soft-fry shallots until translucent.
Add garlic until fragrant.
Toast dry spices with ½ tsp salt briefly.
Add tomatoes and a splash of water; simmer 5–10 minutes to a sauce.
Thin tahini with water and salt for drizzle.
Stir lentils, chopped walnuts, sugar and pomegranate molasses into the pan.
Cook 5–10 minutes more, loosening with water; taste.
Season aubergines; top with mince; drizzle tahini; garnish.
notes: Tags: comfort food,easy,gluten-free,healthy,Middle East-inspired. Original text rewritten for The Starred Kitchen with attribution.
credit: Rewritten for The Starred Kitchen · inspired by Ania (Lazy Cat Kitchen)

title: Vegan paella
ingredients: 10 cm / 4" by 20 cm / 8" piece of kombu
1 vegan stock cube (if not using homemade stock)
2 tablespoon (30 ml) extra virgin olive oil, plus more for grilling
200 g / 7 oz ripe tomato (1 large), peeled and chopped
200 g / 7 oz / 1 slightly heaped cup paella/bomba rice (arborio does good enough job too)
A generous pinch of saffron, dissolved in 2 tbsp hot water
Freshly ground black pepper, to serve
½ cup cooked peas or broad beans (or a mixture of both)
method: If making stock, simmer aromatics in ~750 ml water, covered.
Fry onion in 2 tsp oil in a paella pan ~5 minutes.
Add garlic until soft.
Add tomato, salt, smoked paprika, wine and red pepper.
Cook ~10 minutes until tomatoes break down and pepper softens.
Meanwhile char courgette, fennel and cherry tomatoes on an oiled griddle.
Stir rice into the pan.
Add saffron, saffron water and 500 ml stock; simmer without stirring 10 minutes.
Off heat, cover tightly and rest until rice is tender.
Top with charred veg, peas or beans, olives, artichokes and parsley.
notes: Tags: comfort food,easy,gluten-free. Original text rewritten for The Starred Kitchen with attribution.
credit: Rewritten for The Starred Kitchen · inspired by Ania (Lazy Cat Kitchen)

title: Vegan bun noodles with tofu
ingredients: 4 tbsp / ¼ cup fresh lime juice
1 small garlic clove, finely grated or minced
2 tsp finely grated ginger, to taste
200 g / 7 oz firm (cotton not silken) tofu, pressed and cubed
Peanut oil (or other high smoke oil), for frying (optional)
100 g / 3.5 oz bun rice noodles (or rice vermicelli)
1 baby gem lettuce, leaves shredded roughly
A large handful of mint and coriander leaves
method: Mix the marinade ingredients.
Marinate tofu cubes in a shallow dish with a quarter of the marinade.
Set remaining marinade aside as dressing.
Heat 2 tbsp peanut oil; drain tofu.
Fry until golden on both sides.
Cook noodles per packet; rinse cold.
Blanch sprouts in boiling water seconds; ice bath.
Build bowls with cold noodles, vegetables, sprouts and tofu; herbs and dressing.
notes: Tags: easy,gluten-free,healthy. Original text rewritten for The Starred Kitchen with attribution.
credit: Rewritten for The Starred Kitchen · inspired by Ania (Lazy Cat Kitchen)

title: Vietnamese tofu
ingredients: 2 tbsp vegetable oil (plus more if frying the tofu)
2 Thai red chillies, sliced OR sambal oelek to taste
Two 400 g / 14 oz can of quality peeled plum tomatoes or 6 medium ripe tomatoes, peeled and chopped
¼ tsp ground white pepper (or black if unavailable)
2 tsp coconut sugar (or other), to taste
5 cm / 2" by 10 cm / 4" piece of kombu (optional)
400 g / 14 oz firm (cotton not silken) tofu, pressed well
3 tbsp soy sauce (or tamari for GF version)
2 spring onions, sliced finely, to garnish
Fresh coriander and mint, to garnish
method: Strip tough lemongrass layers; bruise; finely chop bottom 10 cm; reserve tops.
Soft-fry shallots in 2 tbsp oil.
Add lemongrass, garlic, chilli and ginger on low heat until fragrant.
Toast cumin, coriander and most salt briefly.
Add tomatoes; crush; add 2 tinfuls water.
Simmer with lemongrass tops, kombu and optional shiitake.
Cook ~45 minutes until thick; add water if needed.
Discard aromatics; season with white pepper, salt, lime and coconut sugar; blend if desired.
Cube tofu; marinate in soy until absorbed.
Dust with cornflour if frying.
Fry in hot oil until golden; drain.
Or bake 180°C / 355°F 20–25 minutes, turning once.
notes: Tags: Asian-inspired,gluten-free,healthy,tofu. Original text rewritten for The Starred Kitchen with attribution.
credit: Rewritten for The Starred Kitchen · inspired by Ania (Lazy Cat Kitchen)

title: Vegan aubergine curry
ingredients: 60 g / ½ cup pan toasted cashews*, plus more to garnish
10 dry (or fresh ones if you can find them) curry leaves
1 fresh green chilli, sliced (adjust to your tolerance)
¼-½ tsp Kashmiri or regular chilli powder (adjust to your tolerance)
Two 400 ml / 14 oz can of plum tomatoes
6 baby aubergines / eggplants or 2 regular aubergines / eggplants
method: Soak ½ cup cashews or coconut in boiling water.
Pop mustard seeds in hot oil.
Fry nigella, fennel and curry leaves 1–2 minutes.
Soften onion 5–7 minutes.
Add garlic, ginger and chilli until fragrant.
Toast dry spices; splash water if dry.
Add tomatoes; crush gently.
Add ~480 ml water and ½ tsp salt.
Simmer covered until tomatoes break down.
Quarter baby aubergines on the stem, or cube larger ones.
Fry baby aubergines ~10 minutes or roast cubes at 210°C / 410°F ~20 minutes.
Simmer baby aubergines in curry 10–15 minutes until tender.
Lift out; adjust salt, sugar and lime.
Blend drained cashews with sauce until silky.
Return sauce and aubergine to the pan; warm.
Serve with rice or naan, coriander and cashews.
notes: Tags: aubergine,easy,gluten-free,healthy. Original text rewritten for The Starred Kitchen with attribution.
credit: Rewritten for The Starred Kitchen · inspired by Ania (Lazy Cat Kitchen)

title: Lemongrass soup with noodles and greens
ingredients: 1 large shallot, cut into quarters, skin on
½ sheet of kombu (15 cm x 5 cm / 5 in x 2 in ) (optional)
A bunch of fresh coriander stalks (keep the leaves for serving)
8 fresh or frozen Makrut lime leaves, torn
Approx. 2 tsp sea salt, divided (to taste)
Approx. 2 tbsp lime juice, to taste
1 spring onion, sliced finely, to garnish
Chilli oil or condiment like sambal oelek, to taste (optional)
Fresh coriander and mint, to garnish
method: Bruise lemongrass bottoms; discard tops and tough layers.
Simmer stock ingredients (except miso) with 1 tsp salt in ~2 L water.
Gentle boil then low simmer 30 minutes; remove kombu; rest if possible.
Strain, pressing vegetables.
Season with miso, salt and lime.
Cook noodles; toss with 2 tsp sesame oil.
Char pressed tofu on a hot griddle.
Steam broccoli ~7 min and bok choy ~6; ice bath.
Build bowls with noodles, zoodles, tofu and greens; ladle broth; garnish.
notes: Tags: Asian-inspired,comfort food,gluten-free,healthy. Original text rewritten for The Starred Kitchen with attribution.
credit: Rewritten for The Starred Kitchen · inspired by Ania (Lazy Cat Kitchen)

title: Vegan coffee walnut cake
ingredients: 60 ml / ¼ cup maple syrup or other liquid sweetener
60 ml / ¼ cup very strong coffee
195 g / 1½ cups raw cashews, soaked in boiling water for 20 min
180 g / 1½ cups all purpose white flour or all purpose GF flour mix
195 ml / ¾ cup + 1 tbsp plant milk
60 ml / ¼ cup melted refined coconut oil (or other mild tasting oil)
method: Blend maple, vanilla and coffee with a quarter of drained cashews until smooth.
Blend remaining cashews in batches until silky.
Chill frosting hours or overnight.
Heat oven to 180°C / 355°F (160°C fan); oil a 900 g tin.
Mix sifted flour with walnuts, raising agents and sugar.
Fold in wet ingredients until no dry pockets.
Bake 40–45 minutes until a skewer is clean.
Cool completely before frosting and topping with walnuts.
notes: Tags: baking,easy,gluten-free. Original text rewritten for The Starred Kitchen with attribution.
credit: Rewritten for The Starred Kitchen · inspired by Ania (Lazy Cat Kitchen)

title: Savoury vegan breakfast bowl
ingredients: A bunch of cherry tomatoes on the vine
250 g / 9 oz cooked and cooled small potatoes, halved
¼ tsp black salt (has eggy taste), to taste
½ ripe avocado, cut in half
method: Grill oiled vine tomatoes 5–10 minutes until blistered; season.
Fry cold potato halves cut-side down in 2 tsp oil until browned; season.
Wilt spinach with a splash of water; drain.
Gently fry shallot and garlic in 1 tbsp oil.
Scramble tofu with turmeric, black salt and pepper.
Assemble bowls with avocado and optional oil.
notes: Tags: comfort food,easy,gluten-free,healthy,tofu. Original text rewritten for The Starred Kitchen with attribution.
credit: Rewritten for The Starred Kitchen · inspired by Ania (Lazy Cat Kitchen)

title: Green spring salad
ingredients: 60 ml / ¼ cup extra virgin olive oil
2 tablespoon (30 ml) lemon juice, to taste
A handful of fresh mint leaves (approx. 7 g / 0.25 oz), to taste
½ tsp maple syrup or sugar
½ cup frozen petit pois (small peas)
200 g / 7 oz asparagus, wooden ends cut off
method: Blend oil, lemon, mint, mustard and garlic; season with salt, pepper and maple.
Toast almonds; cool and chop.
Boil new potatoes until tender; cool and halve if large.
Cook peas; oil and griddle asparagus; slice courgette thinly.
Toss leaves, gem lettuce and vegetables with dressing.
Finish with almonds.
Serve at once.
notes: Tags: easy,gluten-free,healthy. Original text rewritten for The Starred Kitchen with attribution.
credit: Rewritten for The Starred Kitchen · inspired by Ania (Lazy Cat Kitchen)

title: Sweet potato and black bean bake
ingredients: 1 tsp ground cumin, more to season layers
1½ tsp smoked paprika, more to season layers
1 tsp oregano, more to season layers
Two 400 g / 14 oz tins quality chopped tomatoes
1 tsp salt, more to season layers (to taste!!)
2 large sweet potatoes*, peeled if desired
Two 400 g / 14 oz cans black beans (no BPA and organic if possible), drained
200 g / 7 oz melty vegan cheese, shredded or homemade cashew bechamel
Ripe avocado or store-bought guacamole, to serve (optional)
method: Soft-fry onion in 2 tbsp oil until nearly translucent.
Add garlic 1 minute.
Toast dry spices 1 minute.
Add tomatoes; crush; simmer.
Add a tinful of water; cook until saucy; season.
Heat oven to 180°C / 355°F; oil a baking dish.
Spread 120 ml sauce in the base.
Mandoline sweet potato to 3 mm slices.
Layer overlapping potato; season with salt, oregano and smoked paprika.
Add one tin black beans; salt and cumin.
Repeat potato layer and seasoning.
Add second tin beans; season.
Third potato layer and seasoning.
Top with remaining sauce (~¾ cup).
Cover with foil; bake ~60 minutes until tender.
Add vegan cheese; bake uncovered 10–15 minutes.
notes: Tags: comfort food,easy,gluten-free,healthy,Mexican. Original text rewritten for The Starred Kitchen with attribution.
credit: Rewritten for The Starred Kitchen · inspired by Ania (Lazy Cat Kitchen)

title: Vegan scones
ingredients: 500 g / 4 cups all purpose white wheat flour
A good pinch of fine sea salt
100 g / ½ cup packed fragrance-free (or extra virgin if you don't mind coconut taste) coconut oil at room temperature
Approx. 320 ml / 1 + 1/3 cup almond milk (or any other thin plant milk)
2 tsp olive oil (or other vegetable oil)
method: Sift flour and baking powder.
Mix in sugar and salt.
Rub in chopped coconut oil to a pebbly texture.
Add plant milk gradually; bring together gently without overworking.
Chill dough 15–20 minutes; heat oven to 220°C / 425°F; line a tray.
Roll 2 cm thick on a floured surface.
Cut with a 5 cm fluted cutter without twisting; place on tray.
Gently reroll scraps for more scones.
Glaze tops; sprinkle demerara if using.
Bake 12–15 minutes until risen and golden.
Cool slightly; split and fill with yoghurt and jam.
notes: Tags: baking,comfort food,easy,treat. Original text rewritten for The Starred Kitchen with attribution.
credit: Rewritten for The Starred Kitchen · inspired by Ania (Lazy Cat Kitchen)

title: Vegan BLT salad
ingredients: 2 tbsp tamari (if GF) or soy sauce
¾ tsp smoky sweet (not hot) paprika or a few drops of liquid smoke
200 g / 7 oz tempeh (or firm cotton tofu, pressed)
2 heads of gem lettuce. leaves shredded roughly
250 g / 8.5 oz sweet cherry tomatoes, halved
method: Whisk liquid dressing ingredients.
Stir in minced shallot and capers; season.
Mix tamari, vinegar, maple and paprika for tempeh marinade.
Slice tempeh 3 mm; marinate ≥30 minutes, basting.
Bake at 180°C fan / 200°C conventional 8 minutes per side, brushing with oil.
Cut into bite-size pieces.
Toss potatoes in 2 tsp oil and salt.
Roast 20–30 minutes until browned, stirring once.
Toss lettuce, spinach, tomatoes, avocado, potatoes and tempeh with dressing.
notes: Tags: comfort food,easy,gluten-free. Original text rewritten for The Starred Kitchen with attribution.
credit: Rewritten for The Starred Kitchen · inspired by Ania (Lazy Cat Kitchen)

title: Sweet potato chocolate cake
ingredients: 110 g / ½ cup HOT mashed cooked sweet potato
100 g / 3.5 oz vegan dark chocolate , chopped roughly
3 tbsp maple syrup or plant milk
110 g / ½ cup mashed cooked sweet potato
360 ml / 1½ cup almond milk (or other thin plant milk)
120 ml / ½ cup smooth hazelnut or almond butter
180 g / 1½ cups all purpose wheat flour or GF all purpose flour mix
method: Process ½ cup hot sweet potato with chopped chocolate to a smooth frosting; sweeten or thin as needed.
Heat oven to 180°C / 355°F; line a 900 g tin; lower rack one notch.
Purée ½ cup sweet potato with ½ cup almond milk; blend in remaining wet ingredients.
Sift and mix dry ingredients.
Fold dry into wet in three additions without overmixing.
Spread thick batter in the tin.
Bake 55–60 minutes until a skewer is clean; cool completely before frosting.
notes: Tags: baking,chocolate,gluten-free,oil-free,refined sugar-free. Original text rewritten for The Starred Kitchen with attribution.
credit: Rewritten for The Starred Kitchen · inspired by Ania (Lazy Cat Kitchen)

title: Easy sweet potato dosa
ingredients: 1-2 small red chillies (deseeded for less heat), sliced finely
1 lb / 450 g (about 3 small) sweet potatoes, cubed small
Juice of ½-1 lime, to taste
A pinch of ground turmeric (for colour, optional)
2 tsp oil, plus more for brushing the pan
Thick vegan coconut yoghurt or homemade coconut chutney, to serve
Your preferred sour (like tamarind or lime) chutney or pickle, to serve
method: Pop mustard seeds and curry leaves in hot oil.
Soften onion and chillies; add garlic and ginger until fragrant.
Toast garam masala 1 minute.
Add cubed sweet potato and ~1 cup water; cover and cook ~15 minutes.
Rest covered off heat 5 minutes.
Mash; season with lime and salt.
Mix rice flour, cornflour, salt and optional turmeric.
Whisk in ~2 cups water and oil; rest 10 minutes.
Thin to a runny batter if needed.
Heat an 20 cm non-stick pan; brush with ½ tsp oil.
Ladle ~60 ml batter in a circle from outside in; fill gaps lightly.
Cook until edges lift (~2–3 min); flip 1–2 min.
Fill with sweet potato; coriander; serve with coconut yoghurt and chutney.
notes: Tags: comfort food,gluten-free,healthy,Indian-cuisine. Original text rewritten for The Starred Kitchen with attribution.
credit: Rewritten for The Starred Kitchen · inspired by Ania (Lazy Cat Kitchen)

title: Vegan Thai green curry
ingredients: 2 stalks of lemongrass, soft inner part chopped roughly
4 green Thai chillies (deseeded for less heat)
¼ tsp ground white (or black if unavailable) pepper
Coriander stalks from a big bunch of coriander (use the leaves to serve)
400 ml / 14 oz full fat coconut milk (from a tin)
6 fresh Makrut (previously known as Kaffir) lime leaves
1 tbsp tamari or soy sauce OR vegan fish sauce*, more to taste
½ small butternut squash or a sweet potato, cubed
50 g / 1.5 oz sugar snap peas, sliced on the diagonal
A handful of bean sprouts, blanched
method: Blitz paste ingredients finely in a processor.
Warm oil in a casserole on low heat.
Fry paste 10 minutes, stirring constantly.
Stir in coconut milk.
Add lime leaves and 360 ml stock (more to thin — sauce is traditionally soupy).
Simmer gently 10–15 minutes.
Season with tamari, lime and optional sugar; rest overnight if possible.
Cook vegetables separately (roast squash/aubergine; steam greens) for best colour, or simmer in the sauce.
Serve over jasmine rice with bean sprouts and coriander.
notes: Tags: coconut,comfort food,curry,gluten-free. Original text rewritten for The Starred Kitchen with attribution.

15 g / 0.5 oz dark vegan chocolate , coarsely chopped
method: Slit and pit the dates if needed.
Fill each with a heaping teaspoon of peanut butter.
Finish with chopped chocolate and a pinch of sea salt.

title: Vegan mushroom pasta
ingredients: 3 tablespoon (45 ml) extra virgin olive oil, divided
300 g / 10.5 oz chestnut mushrooms, cleaned and sliced
Salt and black pepper, to taste
A splash of vegan white wine (optional)
A good pinch of chilli flakes
method: Infuse 2 tbsp olive oil with grated garlic.
Toast pine nuts until golden; set aside.
Sauté mushrooms in 1 tbsp oil until caramelised; season; remove.
Wilt spinach with a splash of water; drain.
Cook pasta just shy of al dente; reserve water.
Warm garlic oil in a heavy pan.
Cook garlic ~2 minutes without browning.
Add nutritional yeast, salt and a splash of wine or pasta water.
Toss pasta in the oil; season; add chilli if using.
Return mushrooms and spinach to heat through.
Serve with capers and pine nuts.

title: Buckwheat crepes with cashew cream and rhubarb
ingredients: 225 g / 1½ cups cashews, soaked overnight or in boiling water for 30 minutes
1 tsp vanilla extract or seeds from 1 vanilla pod
3 tsp finely grated ginger, to taste
2 tablespoon (30 ml) maple syrup, to taste
120 g / 1 cup buckwheat flour* or all purpose wheat flour
1 tbsp smooth almond butter (or other smooth nut butter or oil)
method: Chop rinsed cashews (optional for strong blenders).
Blend liquids and vanilla with cashews in quarters until silky.
Season cream with grated ginger.
Chill hours to firm.
Heat oven to 180°C / 355°F.
Slice rhubarb on the diagonal into a dish.
Toss with maple, vanilla and 2 tbsp water.
Bake ~10 minutes until tender but intact.
Whisk flour with plant milk gradually to a smooth batter.
Whisk in thinned almond butter and maple.
Cook crepes in a lightly oiled non-stick pan.
Stack cooked crepes so they stay pliable.
Fill with cream and rhubarb; pistachio optional.
notes: Tags: easy,gluten-free,pancakes,refined sugar-free. Original text rewritten for The Starred Kitchen with attribution.

title: Vegan potato skins with smoky chickpeas
ingredients: 1-2 tsp ancho chilli paste, to taste
1 tsp date syrup or sugar (optional), to taste
Thick vegan yogurt or vegan sour cream, to serve
method: Parboil scrubbed potatoes ~15 minutes; cool.
Soft-fry shallot and garlic in 2 tbsp oil.
Toast spices and ancho paste 1 minute.
Add tomatoes; crush; add a tinful of water; simmer.
Season with salt, pepper, sugar and lime.
Warm chickpeas in the sauce; adjust thickness.
Heat oven to 180°C / 355°F; line a tray.
Halve potatoes; scoop flesh leaving a shell.
Oil and salt the shells; bake ~20 minutes, turning once until crisp.
Fill with chickpeas; yoghurt, pepper and herbs.

title: Chocolate nut bars with salt

75 ml / ¼ cup + 1 tbsp maple syrup
method: Line and grease a small tin.
Heat oven to 160°C / 320°F.
Mix dry ingredients.
Stir in vanilla and maple.
Press firmly into the tin.
Bake ~40 minutes.
Compress and weight while cooling.
Melt chocolate over a double boiler; spread on bars; salt.
Cut when set; store airtight.

title: Winter slaw with mustard orange dressing
ingredients: 3 leaves of Cavolo Nero (aka lacinato / dragon kale)
A small wedge of red cabbage
method: Whisk the first three dressing ingredients until emulsified.
Beat in mustard; season.
Shred cavolo nero, discarding tough stems.
Mandoline-shred sprouts, cabbage, carrot, fennel and kohlrabi.
Slice celery and spring onion; matchstick kohlrabi.
Combine vegetables (hold pomegranate and almonds).
Toss with dressing.
Top with pomegranate and toasted almonds.

title: Vegan spinach and ricotta pierogi
ingredients: 1 medium shallot (+ 2 more for serving if desired), diced finely
method: Soft-fry shallots until translucent and lightly caramelised; reserve some.
Add garlic; cook gently.
Wilt spinach in water in the same pan; cool.
Process tofu with aromatics, lemon, nutritional yeast, salt and nutmeg to a ricotta.
Squeeze spinach dry in muslin.
Mince spinach in the processor.
Fold spinach into ricotta.
Make dough from flour, salt, aquafaba, oil and ~120 ml water; rest.
Roll a quarter of the dough thin; cut rounds; fill and seal.
Boil in batches until they float plus 2–3 minutes.
Optional: pan-fry cooled pierogi in oil until crisp.
Warm reserved shallots; serve alongside.

title: Vegan chocolate torte with amaretto
ingredients: 60 g / ¼ cup smooth almond butter
200 g / 1 cup sugar (use coconut sugar for refined sugar-free version)
2 tbsp toasted almond flakes, to decorate (optional)
method: Heat oven to 180°C / 355°F; grease a 20 cm tin.
Melt chocolate over a water bath.
Blend tofu, amaretto, salt, almond butter, cacao and sugar smooth.
Blend in cooled melted chocolate.
Blend in almond meal and tapioca to a thick batter.
Quickly spread in the tin.
Bake 40 minutes; cool fully; chill 4–8 hours before slicing.

title: Vegan cookie sandwiches
ingredients: 180 gr / approx. 1½ cup all purpose flour, GF all purpose flour mix or buckwheat flour
100 g / 1 cup finely ground almonds or almond meal
150 g / 5.25 oz vegan dark (70% cacao) chocolate
2-3 tbsp / 30-45 ml amaretto liqueur* , to taste
method: Whisk maple, oil, vanilla and almond extract until slightly gelatinous.
Sift in flour with salt; fold.
Fold in almond meal; chill dough 30–60 minutes.
Heat oven to 180°C / 355°F; portion into 30 × 17 g balls.
Flatten on a tray with space between.
Bake 15–18 minutes; cool completely.
Sandwich with ganache; store airtight.
For ganache: chop chocolate into a bowl with coconut milk.
Melt over barely simmering water without stirring until chocolate softens.
Whisk smooth off heat; add maple and amaretto.
Cool; cover; chill hours until pipeable.

title: Roasted brussel sprout pasta
ingredients: 3 tablespoon (45 ml) extra virgin olive oil, divided
Salt and black pepper, to taste
A good pinch of chilli flakes, more to taste (optional)
80 ml / 1/3 cup vegan cream (like Oatly or soya cream), optional
Juice of ½ lemon, plus zest of whole unwaxed lemon
2 tbsp chopped roasted walnuts, to garnish
method: Infuse 2 tbsp oil with 2 grated garlic cloves.
Heat oven to 200°C / 390°F.
Trim and slice sprouts.
Oil and roast in a single layer until browned.
Cook pasta al dente; reserve 60 ml water.
Warm garlic oil with optional chilli.
Cook garlic ~2 minutes without browning.
Add breadcrumbs, nutritional yeast and salt; cook 1 minute.
Optional: stir in vegan cream.
Else emulsify with pasta water.
Season with lemon zest, smoked paprika, salt and pepper; fold in sprouts.
Serve with parsley and walnuts.

title: Miso mushroom bowl
ingredients: 60 ml / ¼ cup rice wine vinegar
Approx. 1 tbsp sugar (add more to taste)
A small piece of ginger, cut into thin matchsticks (optional)
1 tbsp mirin or 2 tsp maple syrup
100 g / 3.5 oz spinach or kale, steamed or stir-fried
method: Simmer vinegar, 60 ml water, salt and sugar.
Pour hot brine over radishes and optional ginger in a jar.
Pickle ≥30 minutes (keeps 2 weeks chilled).
Heat oven to 200°C / 390°F; oil a baking dish.
Thick-slice mushrooms.
Mix miso, rice vinegar, mirin/maple, sesame oil, veg oil and garlic.
Toss mushrooms with ⅔ marinade; bake 15 minutes.
Stir; add remaining marinade; bake ~10 minutes more.
Bowl with rice and greens; spring onion, sesame and pickles.

Maple syrup or stem ginger syrup, to caramelise and to serve

Whisk in plant milk.
Fold in flour and raising agents; thin with a splash of milk if needed.
Warm a non-stick pan moderately.
Brush with ~½ tsp oil.
Cook scant ¼-cup portions 2–3 minutes; flip; cook 1 minute.
Keep warm; serve with caramelised bananas and maple.
Coat banana slices in maple or ginger syrup.
Caramelise both sides on a gentle pan.
Set aside for serving.

title: Vegan Naan Recipe
ingredients: 2¼ tsp active dry yeast ((1 packet. Instant yeast will also work))
½ cup vegan yogurt ((preferably at room temperature))
1 tbsp avocado oil or any neutral oil
4 tablespoons vegan butter ((olive oil works too))
6 cloves garlic ((crushed or put through a garlic press))
2 tablespoons cilantro ((finely chopped. You can sub with another herb like mint))
method: Bloom yeast with 1 cup water and sugar 5 minutes.
Add yoghurt, oil, flour and salt.
Mix to a slightly sticky dough, adding warm water as needed.
Knead briefly; oil bowl; prove ~1 hour until doubled.
Divide into 8 balls; rest covered 20 minutes.
Gently melt garlic herb butter; cook low 15 minutes.
Stretch each ball into a ~15×20 cm oval.
Cook on a ripping-hot cast-iron griddle until bubbled.
Flip once until charred; brush with garlic butter; keep wrapped.

title: Baingan Masala
ingredients: 2 medium potatoes ((Cut into slivers. Use red or yellow potatoes))

Blend onions, tomatoes, ginger-garlic paste and peanuts smooth.
Sputter cumin in oil; add paste on low heat.
Stir in garam masala, turmeric, cayenne/paprika, coriander, cumin and ½ tsp salt.
Cover and cook ~10 minutes until dark and glossy.
Add vegetables and ½–1 cup water; simmer until tender; adjust salt.
Garnish with herbs; serve hot.
