title: Vegan burrito with chipotle tempeh
ingredients: 60 ml / ¼ cup mild olive oil, divided
400 g / 14 oz can of chopped tomatoes
2-3 tsp chipotle chilli paste (I used LUCHITO)
30 ml / 2 tbsp mild olive oil, divided
2 x 400 g / 14 oz cans of black beans
8 x 25 cm / 10" flour tortillas (GF if required)
200 g / 1 cup long grain rice, cooked
hot sauce, I like Chipotle Cholula
method: Set the oven to 200° C / 390° F and line a large baking tray with baking paper. You can skip this step, but I recommend you don't, it makes the mince so much nicer.
Slice tempeh roughly and place it in a food processor. Pulse several times until fairly uniformly ground.
Stir 2 tbsp (30 ml) of olive oil through the tempeh and spread it on the baking tray. Bake for about 30 minutes, giving it a good stir at half way through. Make the sauce while baking the tempeh.

Heat up the remaining 2 tbsp (30 ml) of olive oil in a large frying pan. Add diced onion and sauté on low heat until almost translucent, before adding diced garlic. Continue sautéing until both are translucent.
Making sure the flame is low, add both dry spices and a generous amount of salt. Stir them into the aromatics and continue sautéing for another minute or so.

Next add in chipotle paste (start with 2 tsp and add more if you like more heat) diluted in a tablespoon of water. Sauté for another minute, next add can of tomatoes, more salt and a can worth of water.

Increase the heat to medium and simmer the sauce until thickened. Taste and season with more salt (I like to add a tsp of soy sauce for depth of flavour), pepper and a teaspoon of sugar and a good squeeze of lime to balance all of the flavours out. Stir in baked tempeh and set aside to cool down or store until next day for the flavours to develop.
Cut green parts of spring onions (scallions) off and save for another use, slice the white and white green parts finely.
Preheat 2 tbsp (30 ml) of olive oil in a large frying pan on low heat, add spring onions and sauté until almost translucent before adding garlic.
Once both spring onions and garlic are translucent, add dry spices and a generous amount of salt. Sauté them for another minute or so.
Next add in drained beans and a small splash of water. Season again. Use a fork (or a potato masher) to squash some of the beans down - I like to keep some texture.
Cook until excess water cooks out, taste and season with lime juice and more salt, if needed.
Chop tomatoes into very small dice, chop spring onions and coriander (cilantro) very finely.
Stir chopped tomatoes, chopped spring onions and coriander together.
Season with lime juice, salt and pepper to taste. I also like to add a teaspoon of so of sugar to intensify tomatoes' natural sweetness.
Heat up a tortilla until warm and pliable on a large frying pan.

Place a tortilla in front on you, stack cooked rice (if using), beans, chipotle tempeh, pico de gallo and slices of avocado in the middle, close the sides over the filling then roll tightly - see this video for how to do it well.
Heat up a cast iron skillet or a griddle pan, toast each burrito on the seam side and the opposite side. Cut in half and enjoy with a drizzle of hot sauce, if liked.
notes: Tags: comfort food,easy,gluten-free,healthy
credit: Rewritten for The Starred Kitchen · inspired by Ania (Lazy Cat Kitchen)

title: Roasted vegetable pasta
ingredients: 2 tsp roasted vegetable spice mix (any brand)
a large handful of basil and/or parsley leaves
100 g / 3.5 oz vegan feta or other similar cheese, to serve (optional)
method: Preheat the oven to 220° C / 425° F and grab a baking tray.
Cut aubergine and zucchini into 1.25 cm / 0.5 inch slices, then cut the zucchini slices into halves and aubergine slices into quarters. Cut pepper into large chunks.
Coat in 2 tbsp of olive oil, season with oregano, spice mix and salt and pepper. Bake for 25 minutes, stirring once.

Cut cherry tomatoes into halves so that where the stalk comes out of is on one half. Coat in 1 tbsp of oil, season with 1 tsp oregano, 1 grated garlic clove, 1 tsp of sugar and 1½ tbsp of balsamic. Add to the tin with vegetable and bake for another 10-15 minutes.
Stir veggies through cooked pasta (and chickpeas if using). Sprinkle with chopped herbs and serve with crumbled vegan feta on top.

title: Mango granita
ingredients: 850 g / 30 oz can sweetened mango pulp (I used Indus)
thick coconut yoghurt, to serve (I used The Coconut Collaborative)
method: Combine mango pulp with juice of one lime (about 4 tbsp), stir until homogenous.
Transfer the mixture into a shallow freezer-friendly container. I used a metal one.
Cover the container with a lid and freeze for 1 hour

After 1 hr scrape the sides with a fork until all frozen areas have been broken up. Return to the freezer and keep on doing that every hour, until you get a fluffed up mango granita (see picture above).
Once ready to serve, divide between glasses (chill them for 20 minutes beforehand to help granita stay cold). Top with a dollop of thick coconut yoghurt and sprinkle with lime zest.
